email.description:
Unique email-style login identifier for the new member user.

This value is persisted into the todo_app_memberusers.email column, which is constrained by a unique index. It serves as the primary credential for authentication flows, and must conform to application-level validation rules for acceptable email formats.

During registration the backend verifies that no existing member user already uses the same email. On conflict, the endpoint returns a business-level error rather than exposing low-level database details about the uniqueness violation.

password.description:
Plain text password chosen by the registering member user.

The server consumes this value to derive a secure password_hash that is stored in the todo_app_memberusers.password_hash column. The raw password itself is never persisted and should not be logged or echoed back to the client.

Business rules from the authentication requirements define complexity constraints such as minimum length, required character classes, and rejection of common or compromised passwords. The endpoint enforces these rules and reports validation errors using the global error-handling strategy.

display_name.description:
Optional human-friendly display name for the new member user.

When provided, this value is written to the todo_app_memberusers.display_name column and can be used in user interfaces and logs to present a readable identity. It has no role in authentication or authorization decisions and may be omitted entirely during registration.

Clients may allow the user to customize this value at registration time, or the field can be set later via dedicated profile update operations.

oneOf.description: Non-null client IP address value supplied by the caller.
Null when the client does not provide an IP address explicitly and the server derives it from the connection context.

ip.description:
Optional IP address associated with the client initiating the registration request.

This value is stored in the initial session record for the member user and used for security auditing, anomaly detection, and geo- or device-based checks. It may represent either an IPv4 or IPv6 address.

When omitted or null, the server determines the effective client IP from the underlying network connection details.

href.description:
Full URL of the page or endpoint from which the registration request originates.

This captures the entry point context at the time the new member user account and its initial session are created, including protocol, host, path, and optionally query string.

The value is persisted in the session table associated with the new member user and is used for analytics, security review, or tracing user journeys around sign-up events.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL reported by the client when the registration is initiated.

This represents the previous location from which the user navigated before reaching the registration page or starting the sign-up flow.

The value is stored alongside the session data to support navigation path analysis, marketing attribution, and security investigations.

ITodoAppMemberUserLogin.IRequest.description:
Login request payload for authenticating an existing todoApp member user.

This DTO is consumed by the member user login endpoint that validates credentials against the `todo_app_memberusers` table. It carries the minimal set of information required to perform password-based authentication together with session context metadata.

The `email` and `password` fields represent the member user's credentials. The password is provided in plain text over a secure transport and is never stored directly; the backend compares a secure hash of this value with the `password_hash` column in `todo_app_memberusers`.

The `href` and `referrer` fields capture the connection context at the time of authentication and are required for session tracking and security analytics. The optional `ip` field may be supplied by clients that are able to determine the effective client IP, but the backend can also derive it from the network layer when omitted.

This DTO does not contain any user identifiers such as the member user ID from the database, as those are resolved by the authentication process itself.

email.description:
Email identifier used as the unique login name for the member user.

This value is matched against the `email` column of `todo_app_memberusers`, which has a unique index.

The format must be a syntactically valid email address according to standard email address rules, and business rules may apply additional constraints such as domain restrictions.

password.description:
Plain-text password supplied by the member user for authentication.

The backend hashes this value and compares it against the `password_hash` column in `todo_app_memberusers`. The raw password is never stored.

Password complexity requirements and minimum length constraints are defined in the authentication requirements document and must be enforced during validation.

oneOf.description: Non-null client IP address value supplied by the caller.
Null when the client does not provide an IP address explicitly and the server derives it from the connection context.

ip.description:
Optional IP address associated with the client initiating the login request.

This value is used for session tracking, security auditing, and potential anomaly detection. It may represent either an IPv4 or IPv6 address.

When omitted or null, the server determines the effective client IP from the underlying network connection details.

href.description:
Full URL of the page or endpoint from which the login request originates.

This captures the entry point context at the time of authentication, including protocol, host, path, and optionally query string.

The value is stored in the session record and used for analytics, security review, or tracing user journeys.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL reported by the client when the login is initiated.

This represents the previous location from which the user navigated before reaching the login page or initiating the login flow.

The value is stored alongside the session data to support navigation path analysis and security investigations.

ITodoAppMemberUserRefresh.IRequest.description:
Request payload for refreshing authentication tokens for a member user.

This DTO carries the refresh token previously issued during login or join flows and is used to obtain a new access token (and optionally a new refresh token) without re‑submitting the user’s password. The server validates the token, checks the associated member account status in todo_app_memberusers, and then issues new tokens when appropriate.

Sensitive account data such as password hashes or internal flags are never included in this schema. It only transports the opaque refresh token string from client to server.

refreshToken.description:
Opaque refresh token string issued by the authentication system.

This value is treated as an opaque credential by the client and must be provided exactly as issued. The server uses it to locate and validate the underlying session and member user identity before issuing new tokens.

ITodoAppMemberUserLogout.IResponse.description:
Response returned after successfully logging out the current member user session.

The logout operation invalidates the active session in todo_app_memberuser_sessions by setting its expired_at timestamp and revoking associated tokens. This DTO communicates that the operation has completed and provides simple status information suitable for client‑side handling.

No sensitive account or token information is included. The client should treat any existing access or refresh tokens as unusable after receiving this response.

success.description:
Indicates whether the logout operation for the current session completed successfully.

A value of true means the server has marked the underlying session as expired and revoked related tokens according to its internal rules.

message.description:
Human‑readable message describing the logout result.

Client applications can display this text in notifications or logs to explain that the user has been signed out from the current device or context.

ITodoAppMemberUserLogoutAll.IResponse.description:
Response payload for the global logout operation for member users.

This DTO represents the outcome of a "log out from all devices" action initiated by an authenticated member user. It confirms that all active sessions recorded in the `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` table for the current account have been expired and that any related access or refresh tokens have been invalidated.

The fields focus on conveying whether the operation was successful from the client perspective and summarizing how many sessions were affected, without exposing any sensitive authentication data or internal identifiers.

success.description:
Indicates whether the global logout operation completed successfully from the service perspective.

When `true`, the backend has iterated over all active sessions for the authenticated member user and set `expired_at` appropriately in `todo_app_memberuser_sessions`, and has triggered token invalidation for affected sessions.

When `false`, the operation could not be completed as requested, and the `message` field typically carries a human-readable explanation suitable for client display or logging.

affectedSessionCount.description:
Number of member user sessions that were actively terminated by this global logout invocation.

This value counts only sessions that transitioned from active (no `expired_at` value set) to expired as part of the current request. Sessions that had already been expired before the call are not included.

Clients can use this count for UX messaging (for example, to display how many devices were signed out) and for basic audit confirmation.

oneOf.description:
Human-readable summary of the logout-all result when additional context is available.

Typical examples include phrases such as "Logged out from 3 active sessions" or a short diagnostic note when `success` is `false`. This value is intended for UI display or log entries and is not meant for machine parsing.

Explicitly indicates that there is no additional human-readable message to accompany the `success` flag and `affectedSessionCount`.

Clients should interpret a null message as "no further details provided" and rely solely on `success` and `affectedSessionCount` for outcome handling.

message.description:
Optional human-readable summary of the logout-all result.

The service may return either a non-null string with additional context about the operation or `null` to indicate that no extra message is provided beyond `success` and `affectedSessionCount`. API producers should choose exactly one of these shapes for each response, and clients should treat the absence of a non-null message as an indication that no further explanation is available.

ITodoAppMemberUserChangePassword.IReques.description:
Request payload for changing the password of an authenticated member user.

This DTO is used by the password change endpoint for member users backed by the `todo_app_memberusers` table. It carries the current password for verification against the stored `password_hash` and the new password that should replace it after passing complexity and policy checks.

All authentication context, including which member user is performing the change, is derived from the current authenticated session and associated token. No user identifiers or session identifiers are included in this request body; those values are resolved server-side from the security context.

currentPassword.description:
The member user's current password in plain text as entered in the password change form.

The backend uses this value only for verification against the stored `password_hash` in `todo_app_memberusers` using the configured hashing algorithm. It is never persisted in plain text and must be handled in memory only for the duration of verification.

If this value does not match the existing credentials, the operation fails and may increment `failed_login_count` according to authentication policy.

newPassword.description:
The desired new password for the member user, in plain text as entered by the user.

This value is validated against the password complexity rules and security policies defined in the authentication requirements (for example, minimum length, required character classes, and disallowed patterns). On acceptance, the backend hashes this password and stores the result in the `password_hash` column of `todo_app_memberusers`.

The plain text value itself is never stored and should be cleared from memory as soon as the hashing and update steps are complete.

ITodoAppMemberUserChangePassword.IRespon.description:
Response payload returned after a member user has requested a password change.

This type communicates the outcome of the password change process initiated by an authenticated member user. It does not expose any credential or internal security fields from the todo_app_memberusers or todo_app_memberuser_sessions tables.

The response indicates whether the password update and associated session invalidation have completed successfully, and optionally carries a brief, user-facing message describing the result. It is intentionally minimal to avoid leaking security-sensitive implementation details.

success.description:
Flag indicating whether the password change operation has completed successfully.

When true, the service has validated the current password, enforced password complexity rules for the new password, updated the password_hash field for the authenticated member user, reset failed_login_count, updated updated_at, and expired relevant sessions in todo_app_memberuser_sessions.

When false, the password change was rejected due to validation failure, incorrect current password, or another business rule, and no credential changes were persisted.

message.description:
Optional human-readable explanation of the password change result.

This property itself is optional: when present, it is always a non-null string that can be displayed directly in the UI or recorded in logs. On success, it may contain a short confirmation message; on failure, it may provide a high-level reason why the operation could not be completed, without revealing sensitive authentication or policy details.

Clients should treat the absence of this property as "no additional message provided" rather than as an error condition.

ITodoAppAdminUser.IJoin.description:
Request payload for registering a new administrative user account in the todoApp service.

This DTO is used by the POST /auth/adminUser/join endpoint to create a new row in the todo_app_adminusers table. It collects the minimal business data required to provision an admin account: a unique login identifier in the form of an email address, a raw password that will be hashed into the password_hash column, and an optional display name for use in administrative consoles and logs.

The backend is responsible for enforcing uniqueness of the email value, validating the password against the authentication and password complexity rules, initializing failed_login_count, status, created_at, updated_at, and leaving deleted_at as null. The raw password is never stored directly; only a derived password_hash is persisted in the database.

email.description:
Login identifier for the administrative user account.

This value is stored in the email column of the todo_app_adminusers table and must be unique across all admin users, enforced by the unique index on that column. It is used both for authentication and for administrative communication channels, and must be validated as a syntactically correct email address before account creation.

password.description:
Plain-text password chosen by the administrative user during registration.

This value is never stored directly in the database. The service hashes it into a secure password_hash according to the authentication requirements before saving the new admin row. The password must satisfy the password complexity rules defined for admin users, such as minimum length and required character classes.

display_name.description:
Optional human-friendly display name for the administrative user.

When provided, this value is persisted in the display_name column of the todo_app_adminusers table and used in admin consoles, logs, and audit trails to make it easier to recognize who performed administrative actions. If omitted, the system may derive a suitable fallback from the email or other context.

ITodoAppAdminUser.description:
Administrative user account entity for the todoApp service.

This type represents a single administrative user stored in the todo_app_adminusers Prisma model. It captures identity, credential metadata, profile labeling, account status, and audit timestamps required for operating and supervising the todo application.

Admin users are distinct from member users and guests. They own privileged capabilities exposed through separate admin APIs, and their sessions are tracked in the todo_app_adminuser_sessions table for security auditing and anomaly detection.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the administrative user account.

This value corresponds to the primary key id column in the todo_app_adminusers table and uniquely identifies an administrative actor across the entire system.

email.description:
Administrative login email address of the user.

This value maps to the email column in the todo_app_adminusers table and must be unique across all admin accounts. It is used for authentication and administrative communication channels.

display_name.description:
Optional human‑friendly display name for the administrator.

When present, this value comes from the display_name column in todo_app_adminusers and is shown in administrative consoles, logs, and audit reports to make individual admin accounts easier to recognize.

status.description:
Lifecycle and accessibility status of the admin account.

This field reflects the status column in todo_app_adminusers and distinguishes between states such as active, inactive, disabled, or logically deleted, according to business rules configured in the service.

failed_login_count.description:
Current counter of consecutive failed login attempts for this admin user.

The value is stored in the failed_login_count column of todo_app_adminusers and is used to implement security features such as lockout thresholds and rate limiting around authentication attempts.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent successful login performed by this admin user.

This value maps to the last_login_at column in todo_app_adminusers and is null when the administrator has never logged in successfully.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of this administrative user record.

The value comes from the created_at column in todo_app_adminusers and represents when the admin identity was first provisioned in the system.

updated_at.description:
Last update timestamp for this administrative user record.

This maps to the updated_at column in todo_app_adminusers and is automatically refreshed whenever mutable account fields such as email, display_name, or status are changed.

deleted_at.description:
Logical deletion or deactivation timestamp for this administrative user.

The field corresponds to deleted_at in todo_app_adminusers. When non‑null, it indicates that the admin account has been logically deleted or deactivated while the underlying record remains available for potential recovery or auditing.

ITodoAppAdminUser.IAuthorized.description:
Authorized administrative user context returned by join, login, and refresh operations.

This DTO combines the stable identity of the admin user with the current authorization token bundle so that clients can both display who is logged in and store credentials for subsequent calls.

The payload is produced after successful execution of adminUser authentication flows against todo_app_adminusers, and it respects the token and session lifecycle described in the authentication and session requirements document.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated admin user.

This is copied from todo_app_adminusers.id and is used by clients and downstream services as the primary reference to the admin actor.

email.description:
Email address of the authenticated admin user.

Matches the email column in todo_app_adminusers and serves as the login identifier as well as a human‑readable label for the current admin session.

display_name.description:
Optional display name of the authenticated admin.

When provided, clients can show this value in navigation bars, dashboards, and audit views instead of the raw email address. Null means that no explicit display name has been configured.

status.description:
Current status of the admin account.

Allows clients and middleware to adapt behavior when an account is inactive, disabled, or otherwise restricted, even though a token has just been issued. This mirrors the status column of todo_app_adminusers at the time of token generation.

failed_login_count.description:
Current counter of consecutive failed login attempts for this admin user.

The value is stored in the failed_login_count column of todo_app_adminusers and is used to implement security features such as lockout thresholds and rate limiting around authentication attempts.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent successful login performed by this admin user.

This value maps to the last_login_at column in todo_app_adminusers and is null when the administrator has never logged in successfully.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of this administrative user record.

The value comes from the created_at column in todo_app_adminusers and represents when the admin identity was first provisioned in the system.

updated_at.description:
Last update timestamp for this administrative user record.

This maps to the updated_at column in todo_app_adminusers and is automatically refreshed whenever mutable account fields such as email, display_name, or status are changed.

deleted_at.description:
Logical deletion or deactivation timestamp for this administrative user.

The field corresponds to deleted_at in todo_app_adminusers. When non‑null, it indicates that the admin account has been logically deleted or deactivated while the underlying record remains available for potential recovery or auditing.

ITodoAppAdminUser.ILogin.description:
Login request payload for authenticating an administrative user.

Clients submit this DTO to the adminUser login endpoint when an existing admin wants to obtain fresh authorization tokens using their credentials. It carries the login identifier and password, along with the connection context required to create audit and rate‑limiting records.

On the server side, the credentials are checked against todo_app_adminusers, and each attempt is recorded into todo_app_login_attempts with fields such as login_identifier, actor_type, ip, user_agent, succeeded, and failure_reason populated according to the outcome.

email.description:
Login identifier for the admin user.

This value is matched against the email column of todo_app_adminusers after applying any normalization rules defined in the authentication requirements. It must uniquely identify the administrative account being authenticated.

password.description:
Plain‑text password for the admin user being authenticated.

The server never stores this value directly. Instead, it uses it to derive and compare a secure hash against the password_hash column of todo_app_adminusers, following the password‑handling rules for the service.

ip.description:
Optional IP address from which the login request originates.

When provided, this is used to populate the ip column in todo_app_login_attempts and to support abuse detection and rate limiting. If omitted or null, the server may infer the remote address from the connection layer instead.

href.description:
Full URL that the admin user accessed when initiating this login.

Stored alongside the login attempt to reconstruct navigation paths into the admin interface and to support security investigations of unusual entry points.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL reported by the client at the time of the login attempt.

Captured in login attempt records to help trace how the admin navigation led to the authentication action, which can be useful in auditing and incident analysis.

user_agent.description:
Optional user agent string of the client performing the login.

When provided, this value is recorded into todo_app_login_attempts.user_agent and can be used to distinguish between browsers, devices, and automated tools during security reviews.

ITodoAppAdminUser.IRefresh.description:
Request body for refreshing authentication tokens for an administrative user.

This DTO is used by the POST /auth/adminUser/refresh operation to request new authorization tokens based on an existing refresh token, without resubmitting admin credentials. It represents the minimal business data the client must provide so that the backend can validate token integrity, correlate it to a concrete admin identity in todo_app_adminusers, and apply the token lifecycle and security rules defined for the todoApp service.

The structure is intentionally compact and does not include any actor identifiers or session identifiers that are managed by the authentication infrastructure. All account state checks, session linkage, and login attempt analysis are performed on the server side using the supplied token value.

refresh_token.description:
Opaque refresh token previously issued to the admin user during login or join.

The value is treated as an application-managed token that encodes or references the session and identity context for a todo_app_adminusers row. The client must send it exactly as originally received, without modification or partial truncation. The backend validates the token, checks expiry and revocation state, and ensures the underlying admin account is still active and not logically deleted before issuing new authorization tokens.

ITodoAppGuestUser.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination parameters for listing guest user identities from the todo_app_guestusers table.

This DTO is used by the PATCH /todoApp/guestUser/guestUsers endpoint to drive filtered, paginated queries over guest user records. It allows internal tools or backoffice processes to narrow the result set by creation date, sort the data for analysis, and control page sizing when browsing large volumes of unauthenticated visitor identities.

All fields are optional to support flexible querying. When omitted, the backend applies sensible defaults such as returning the first page, using a standard page size, and ordering by creation time descending. The DTO does not include any direct actor identifiers or sensitive authentication information; it is purely a query envelope around the todo_app_guestusers primary entity.

page.description:
1-based index of the page to retrieve from the guest user list.

When provided, this value selects which subset of the filtered result set should be returned. A value of 1 refers to the first page. If omitted, the implementation should default to the first page for convenience. Values less than 1 should be rejected or normalized according to the service's validation rules.

limit.description:
Maximum number of guest user summary records to include in a single page of results.

This parameter allows callers to control page size for list views and analytical tools. When omitted, the backend uses a configured default page size that balances performance and usability. Extremely large limits may be capped by server-side constraints to protect the system from excessive load.

created_from.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the guest user creation timestamp range filter in ISO 8601 date-time format.

When set, only guest user records whose created_at column in todo_app_guestusers is greater than or equal to this value are considered for inclusion. This parameter is typically used to analyze new visitor cohorts starting from a specific point in time.

created_to.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the guest user creation timestamp range filter in ISO 8601 date-time format.

When set, only guest user records whose created_at column in todo_app_guestusers is less than or equal to this value are considered for inclusion. Combined with created_from, this field defines a time window used to restrict the cohort of guest users returned by the search.

order_by.description:
Logical field name to use when ordering the guest user result set.

Typical values include created_at or updated_at so that consumers can view the newest or most recently changed guest identities first. The exact set of allowed values is enforced by the backend; unsupported fields should result in validation errors rather than silent acceptance.

order_direction.description:
Direction in which to apply the sort defined by order_by.

Common values are asc for ascending order and desc for descending order. When omitted, the backend usually defaults to descending order by creation time so that the most recent guest user records appear first in list views.

ITodoAppGuestUser.description:
Detailed representation of a guest user identity tracked by the todoApp service.

This DTO maps directly to a single row in the `todo_app_guestusers` Prisma table, which represents an unauthenticated visitor interacting with the todo application. It includes the primary identifier, optional display name, and full lifecycle timestamps so that internal tools and diagnostic workflows can inspect how guest identities are created and updated over time.

Unlike end‑user facing resources, guest user identities are a system‑managed concept used for correlation and analysis rather than direct manipulation. This detail view is primarily used by backoffice, monitoring, and support tooling as the response body for `GET /todoApp/guestUser/guestUsers/{guestUserId}` and any similar internal integrations that require the complete stored state of a guest user record.

id.description:
Primary key of the guest user record in the `todo_app_guestusers` table.

This value uniquely identifies a conceptual guest identity within the system and is used by internal tools or subsequent API calls whenever a specific guest user record must be referenced.

It is generated and managed exclusively by the backend and is never supplied directly by clients.

oneOf.description:
Display name or nickname associated with the guest user.

This value is intended for human‑friendly labelling in internal consoles, logs, or analytics dashboards when a recognizable label is preferred over a raw identifier.

It is optional and may be omitted or null when the system has not captured any meaningful label for the guest context.

No display name is recorded for this guest user.

Null indicates that the guest identity has no associated nickname or human‑readable label stored in the `display_name` column.

display_name.description:
Optional display name for this guest user.

When present, it provides a human‑readable nickname that can be presented in administrative tooling or analytics.

When absent (null), the guest identity is typically referenced only by its id or by external context such as device or browser information.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this guest user record was created in the `todo_app_guestusers` table.

Stored as an ISO 8601 date‑time value in UTC. This marks the first time the system recorded this guest identity and is commonly used for cohort analysis or for ordering guest records by creation time.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this guest user record was last updated in the `todo_app_guestusers` table.

Stored as an ISO 8601 date‑time value in UTC. This value changes whenever mutable fields such as `display_name` are modified and is useful for understanding how recently the guest profile was touched by the system.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp marking when this guest user record was logically deleted.

Stored as an ISO 8601 date‑time value in UTC. Once set, the record is considered removed from normal operational use but may remain in the database for audit or analytical purposes.

The guest user record is currently active and has not been logically deleted.

Null indicates that the row is considered part of the active dataset.

deleted_at.description:
Logical deletion timestamp for the guest user record.

When non‑null, the value indicates the moment the guest identity was retired from normal use while possibly remaining available for internal audit or analysis.

When null, the record is treated as active and may still participate in reporting or correlation features.

ITodoAppGuestUserMetadata.description:
Additional metadata associated with a guest user identity managed by the todoApp backend.

This object represents system-managed, non-critical attributes that help the backend correlate and manage guest contexts across requests and sessions. It is not directly mapped to a single Prisma model table; instead, it is a stable public projection of commonly useful metadata fields that may be derived from request headers, connection details, or related logging structures.

The schema intentionally focuses on a small set of well-understood, low-risk fields that are safe to expose through APIs. Backends may internally capture additional metadata for operational purposes, but only the properties defined here are surfaced to API consumers, ensuring a clear and stable contract. Future versions can introduce new metadata fields through separate schema extensions without breaking existing integrations.

Client applications typically use this metadata for diagnostics, customer support, and coarse-grained analytics, rather than for core business logic. Values may be absent or partially populated, depending on what information was actually observed on the underlying connection.

userAgent.description:
User agent string reported by the guest user's client, if captured.

This value typically comes from the HTTP `User-Agent` header and may include browser name, version, operating system, and device information. It is useful for diagnostics and customer support when analyzing guest interactions by device type, browser family, or platform characteristics.

Because user agent strings are free-form and controlled by the client, they should not be trusted for security-sensitive decisions. They are best treated as informational metadata and may be missing, truncated, or spoofed.

ipAddress.description:
IP address observed for the guest user's connection, if recorded.

The value is represented as a textual IPv4 or IPv6 address (for example, `203.0.113.10` or `2001:db8::1`). It is typically derived from the network layer or from reverse proxies and load balancers configured in front of the todoApp service.

This metadata is intended primarily for security review, traffic analysis, and troubleshooting. It may not be present for all records, and it should not be treated as a stable identifier because addresses can change over time, be shared by multiple users, or be masked by NAT or VPN technologies.

ITodoAppMemberuserSession.IRequest.description:
Filter and pagination parameters for listing authentication sessions of a specific member user in the todoApp service.

This DTO is used as the request body for the session history search endpoint that lists records from the subsidiary table `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` for a given owner in `todo_app_memberusers`. It allows clients to express time range and activity constraints and standard paging options without ever carrying any authentication or actor identity fields.

The structure is intentionally minimal: all actor and ownership information is derived from the authenticated principal and the `memberUserId` path parameter, while this object focuses purely on search behavior such as whether only active (non‑expired) sessions should be returned and which date window to inspect.

page.description:
1‑based index of the page of session records to retrieve.

Clients use this value together with `limit` to navigate through long session histories. When omitted, the server typically assumes the first page.

This parameter affects only the pagination window and has no impact on security or authorization.

limit.description:
Maximum number of session records to include in a single page of results.

This value is used together with `page` to implement offset‑based pagination over `todo_app_memberuser_sessions`, leveraging the index on `[todo_app_memberuser_id, created_at]` for efficient ordering.

The backend enforces an upper bound to prevent excessively large result sets that could impact performance.

activeOnly.description:
When true, restricts the query to sessions that are currently active.

An active session is one whose `expired_at` column in `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` is null or is strictly later than the current time, according to the business rules of the authentication subsystem.

When false or omitted, both active and expired sessions may be returned, subject to other filters.

oneOf.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) of the creation timestamp window for sessions to include.

When provided, only rows whose `created_at` column in `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` is greater than or equal to this value are considered. The timestamp must be expressed in ISO 8601 `date-time` format.

This filter is optional and can be combined with `createdTo` to form a closed interval.

Indicates that no lower bound constraint is applied to the `created_at` field when filtering sessions.

Use this when the client wants to start from the earliest available session history.

createdFrom.description:
Optional inclusive lower bound for the session creation timestamp filter.

This field corresponds to the `created_at` column in `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` and allows clients to limit the search to more recent sessions when investigating security incidents or recent activity.

Provide a value in ISO 8601 `date-time` format or null to omit the constraint.

oneOf.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) of the creation timestamp window for sessions to include.

When provided, only rows whose `created_at` column in `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` is less than or equal to this value are returned. The timestamp must follow ISO 8601 `date-time` format.

This filter is optional and can be combined with `createdFrom` for a bounded interval.

Indicates that no upper bound constraint is applied to the `created_at` field when filtering sessions.

Use this when the client wants to include all sessions from the lower bound onward or the entire history if `createdFrom` is also omitted.

createdTo.description:
Optional inclusive upper bound for the session creation timestamp filter.

This field directly targets the `created_at` column in `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` and is typically used to close a time window when reviewing sessions around a particular incident or time frame.

Provide a value in ISO 8601 `date-time` format or null to omit the constraint.

ITodoAppMemberuserSession.description:
Detailed representation of a single authentication session for a todoApp member user.

This DTO mirrors one row from the subsidiary Prisma model `todo_app_memberuser_sessions`, which captures per‑session connection context and lifetime information for a member user in `todo_app_memberusers`. It is used as the response body for the detail endpoint that fetches a specific session identified by `sessionId` within the scope of its owning member user.

The type exposes only session‑level fields that are safe for the authenticated owner or a privileged administrator to see: IP address, entry URL, referrer, temporal metadata needed for audit or self‑inspection, and a lightweight summary of the owning member user account for contextual display. It deliberately does not include any authentication tokens or sensitive credential material, which are managed separately by the authentication subsystem.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the member user session.

This value corresponds directly to the primary key `id` column of the `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` table and uniquely distinguishes this specific authenticated context from all other sessions.

Clients use this identifier when requesting details about a particular session or when rendering audit trails that link to more detailed views.

ip.description:
IP address from which the member user established this session.

The value is captured from the incoming request at the time of successful authentication and stored in the `ip` column of `todo_app_memberuser_sessions`. It may represent either the direct client IP or a proxy‑adjusted address depending on server infrastructure.

This field is primarily used for security review, anomaly detection, and allowing users to recognize unfamiliar access locations.

href.description:
Full URL that the member user visited when this session was created.

This value is stored in the `href` column of `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` and typically includes the scheme, host, path, and query string. It represents the entry point into the application at the moment of login.

It is useful for understanding which part of the application initiated the session, for example a login page, an auto‑login redirect, or a specific deep link.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL reported by the client when the session was established.

Persisted in the `referrer` column of `todo_app_memberuser_sessions`, this field captures the page that led to the login or session creation request, when available.

It helps operators and end users analyze navigation flows, marketing campaign effectiveness, or potential phishing attempts if the referrer looks suspicious.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this session record was created.

The value comes directly from the `created_at` column of `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` and marks the time of successful authentication for this particular session.

It is used for temporal ordering of sessions in history views and for computing the age of a session.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp indicating when this session became invalid.

This value maps to the `expired_at` column of `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` and is set when the session is explicitly logged out or automatically expired by the authentication subsystem.

When present, it allows clients and operators to see exactly when a session stopped being usable.

Indicates that the session has not yet been marked as expired.

A null value in `expired_at` means the session is currently considered active by the persistence layer, although real‑time enforcement may also consider token expiry and other factors managed outside this table.

expired_at.description:
Optional timestamp indicating when the session expired, if it is no longer active.

This field reflects the `expired_at` column of `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` and distinguishes active sessions (null value) from those that have been terminated.

Consumers can use this to visually mark closed sessions and to filter out long‑expired ones in application logic when necessary.

memberUser.description:
Lightweight summary of the member user who owns this session.

This association is derived from the foreign key `todo_app_memberuser_id` in the `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` table, which references `todo_app_memberusers.id`. Instead of exposing the raw foreign key, the DTO provides a minimal projection of the owning member user using `ITodoAppMemberUser.ISummary`.

Including this summary allows security dashboards, account management UIs, and audit tooling to show which account a session belongs to alongside connection metadata, while avoiding circular references and keeping the response payload focused on session context.

ITodoAppAdminUser.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing administrative user account.

This type defines the subset of fields from the todo_app_adminusers model that can be changed after the account has been created. It is used as the request body for the PUT /todoApp/adminUser/adminUsers/{adminUserId} endpoint.

All properties are optional, following a partial‑update pattern. Server‑side logic is responsible for enforcing business rules such as allowed status transitions, email uniqueness, and security policies when resetting failed login counters or applying logical deletions via deleted_at.

email.description:
New email address for the administrative user.

When provided, this value updates the email column in todo_app_adminusers. The backend must ensure that the new email remains unique across all admin accounts and that any associated authentication or notification workflows are updated accordingly.

display_name.description:
New human‑friendly display name for the administrative user.

Supplying a non‑null value updates the display_name column in todo_app_adminusers. Sending null clears any existing display name, allowing the account to fall back to other identifiers in user interfaces and logs.

status.description:
Updated status for the administrative account.

This value overwrites the status column in todo_app_adminusers. The application must validate that the requested transition is allowed, for example when moving between active, inactive, disabled, or logically deleted states.

failed_login_count.description:
Override value for the failed login attempt counter.

When present, this field updates the failed_login_count column in todo_app_adminusers. Typical use cases include resetting the counter to zero after a lockout review or adjusting it during security operations.

last_login_at.description:
Administrative override of the last successful login timestamp.

Although normally managed automatically by the authentication subsystem, this field allows privileged tools to correct or migrate last_login_at values stored in todo_app_adminusers when necessary.

deleted_at.description:
Logical deletion or reactivation marker for the admin account.

Setting this value updates the deleted_at column in todo_app_adminusers. A non‑null timestamp indicates logical deletion or deactivation, while explicitly sending null can be used by privileged tooling to restore an account that was previously marked as deleted.

ITodoAppAdminUser.IRequest.description:
Search, filtering, sorting, and pagination parameters for querying administrative users.

This DTO is used as the request body of the admin user search endpoint that returns a paginated list of admin user summaries. It does not map directly to a single Prisma model but instead aggregates query concerns for `todo_app_adminusers`, such as keyword search, status filters, and date range constraints.

Clients use this type to construct rich queries for backoffice consoles, enabling operators to quickly locate admin accounts by identity, lifecycle status, or creation time windows while controlling result ordering and page size.

page.description:
Zero-based page index to retrieve.

Represents which page of results to return from the admin user list. Page 0 usually means the first page of results.

If omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default such as 0.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return in a single page.

Controls the page size for the admin user search endpoint. Implementations should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large responses.

If omitted, the service should use a default page size defined by system configuration.

keyword.description:
Free-text keyword for searching across primary identity fields.

Typically applied to columns like `email` and `display_name` in `todo_app_adminusers`. When provided, the backend should perform a case-insensitive partial match where appropriate.

When null or omitted, no keyword-based filtering is applied.

status.description:
Filter for admin account lifecycle status.

When set, this restricts the search to records in `todo_app_adminusers` whose `status` column matches the provided value. Business logic defines the allowed status values.

If null or omitted, results are not filtered by status.

created_from.description:
Lower bound of the admin account creation time range filter.

When provided, only admin users with `created_at` greater than or equal to this timestamp in `todo_app_adminusers` are included in the results.

If null or omitted, no lower bound is applied to the creation time.

created_to.description:
Upper bound of the admin account creation time range filter.

When set, the search includes only admin users whose `created_at` is less than or equal to this timestamp.

If null or omitted, no upper bound is applied to the creation time.

order_by.description:
Name of the field used to sort admin user results.

Typical values correspond to sortable columns on `todo_app_adminusers`, such as `created_at`, `email`, or `status`. The backend must validate that the value refers to an allowed sort key.

When null or omitted, a default sort order, such as by `created_at` descending, should be applied.

order_direction.description:
Direction of sorting for the admin user results.

Commonly expects values like `asc` or `desc` to indicate ascending or descending order. The service should validate and normalize this value when applying the sort.

If null or omitted, the default direction, typically `desc`, should be used.

ITodoAppAdminUser.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of an administrative user account in the todoApp service.

This summary representation is optimized for list views, reference embedding, and administrative overviews where the full admin user record is not required. It exposes only non-sensitive identification and status fields and strictly excludes all password-related and other confidential data.

Use this type whenever you need to show who an admin is in tables, logs, audit records, or selection dropdowns, without leaking internal security information or verbose metadata.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin user.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `todo_app_adminusers` table. It is used to uniquely reference an administrative actor across the todoApp service, including in audit logs and sessions.

email.description:
Login email of the admin user used as a unique identifier.

This corresponds to the `email` column of `todo_app_adminusers` and is guaranteed to be unique. It is suitable for display in administrative consoles and search results, but must never be used as a substitute for the primary key in internal relations.

display_name.description:
Optional human-friendly display name for the admin user.

When present, this name is preferred for UI display in place of the raw email address. When null, clients should gracefully fall back to using the email or other identifier.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the admin account.

This maps to the `status` column of `todo_app_adminusers`. Typical application-level values include states such as `active`, `inactive`, `disabled`, or `deleted`. Clients can use this field to filter or highlight accounts, but should not attempt to enforce business rules purely on the client side.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent successful login for this admin user.

This corresponds to the `last_login_at` column in `todo_app_adminusers`. It is null when the administrator has never logged in successfully. When present, it helps operators understand recent activity for the account.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this admin user account record was created.

This maps to the `created_at` field of `todo_app_adminusers` and represents when the administrator identity was provisioned in the system. It is useful for sorting and auditing purposes.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this admin user account record was last updated.

This corresponds to the `updated_at` column of `todo_app_adminusers`. It is refreshed whenever profile, credential metadata, or status fields are changed, and helps identify stale or recently modified accounts.

ITodoAppAdminuserSession.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an admin user authentication session in the todoApp service.

This type captures the essential contextual fields of an administrative session, such as the owning admin user, connection origin, and key timestamps. It is designed for use in security dashboards, audit listings, and monitoring tools where many session records must be rendered efficiently.

The summary intentionally omits any credential material and focuses on connection metadata and timestamps so that operators can review and investigate admin activity without exposing sensitive information.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin user session.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `todo_app_adminuser_sessions` table, and uniquely identifies a single authenticated session instance for an admin user.

todo_app_adminuser_id.description:
Raw foreign key identifier of the administrative user who owns this session.

This value maps directly to the `todo_app_adminuser_sessions.todo_app_adminuser_id` column and points to the primary key of the related admin account in the `todo_app_adminusers` table.

It is primarily useful for low‑level debugging, correlation with other audit and log records, or internal tooling that needs to work with identifiers rather than expanded summary objects. In most UI scenarios, clients should rely on the richer `adminUser` summary object for display and user interaction while treating this field as an implementation detail.

adminUser.description:
Summary of the administrative user who owns this session.

This object corresponds to the admin account referenced by `todo_app_adminuser_sessions.todo_app_adminuser_id` and provides key identity and classification information (such as display name and status) needed for security review without exposing low-level credential fields.

ip.description:
Client IP address recorded when the admin session was created.

This field maps to the `ip` column of `todo_app_adminuser_sessions` and is used for security analysis, anomaly detection, and forensic investigation of administrative access patterns.

href.description:
Full URL that the admin user accessed at the moment this session was established.

This corresponds to the `href` column in `todo_app_adminuser_sessions`. It typically represents the entry point into the admin area and helps operators understand which interface or environment the administrator connected through.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL reported by the client when the admin session was created.

This field maps to the `referrer` column of `todo_app_adminuser_sessions`. It records the origin page that led to the session-creating request and is useful for tracing navigation paths into administrative features.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this admin user session record was created.

This corresponds to the `created_at` column of `todo_app_adminuser_sessions` and represents the time of successful authentication for this session.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when this admin user session was terminated or expired, if applicable.

This maps to the `expired_at` column of `todo_app_adminuser_sessions`. While the session remains active, this field is null. Once the session ends, it records when the session was explicitly terminated or reached its configured expiration.

ITodoAppAdminuserSession.IRequest.description:
Search and filter DTO for querying admin user authentication sessions.

This type is used as the request body for the PATCH /todoApp/adminUser/adminUsers/{adminUserId}/sessions endpoint. It allows callers to specify pagination, temporal filtering, and simple status flags when listing sessions for a particular administrative user.

The fields are intentionally generic so that server‑side implementation can map them to appropriate where, orderBy, and pagination clauses against the todo_app_adminuser_sessions model without exposing internal query structures directly.

page.description:
Page index for paginated session results.

The value represents the 1‑based page number to retrieve when listing admin sessions. If omitted, the backend applies a sensible default such as page 1.

limit.description:
Maximum number of session records to return in a single page.

This value controls the page size and should respect server‑side upper bounds to protect performance when querying todo_app_adminuser_sessions.

from_created_at.description:
Lower bound for the session creation timestamp filter.

When provided, only sessions whose created_at is greater than or equal to this datetime will be included in the result set for the specified admin user.

to_created_at.description:
Upper bound for the session creation timestamp filter.

When present, only sessions whose created_at is less than or equal to this datetime will be returned for the targeted admin user.

only_active.description:
Flag indicating whether to restrict results to currently active sessions.

If true, the backend should return only sessions where expired_at is null. If false or omitted, both active and expired sessions may be included depending on other filters.

sort_created_at_desc.description:
Sorting preference for created_at timestamps in the session list.

When true, sessions should be ordered from newest to oldest by created_at. When false, a chronological ascending order may be applied instead. If omitted, the server chooses a sensible default ordering.

ITodoAppAdminuserSession.description:
Administrative authentication session entity for todoApp admin users.

This schema models a single row from the `todo_app_adminuser_sessions` Prisma table. Each instance represents one authenticated admin session, including the connection context and lifecycle timestamps used for audit and security analysis.

At the database level the Prisma model also includes a foreign key column `todo_app_adminuser_id` that links each session to its owning admin account in `todo_app_adminusers`. That relational column is kept internal to the persistence layer and is not exposed as a top-level DTO property; instead, APIs use path parameters such as `adminUserId` together with the `id` property to scope and retrieve sessions safely.

Sessions are created and managed by the authentication subsystem rather than by client APIs. They capture the IP address, entry URL, referrer URL, creation time, and optional expiration time of the session, enabling detailed audit trails and security monitoring without exposing credential material.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin user session.

This value corresponds to the primary key `id` column of the `todo_app_adminuser_sessions` table. It uniquely identifies one authentication session record for an admin user across the entire todoApp system and is used together with the path-level `adminUserId` to ensure that lookups only return sessions belonging to the specified administrative account.

ip.description:
IP address from which the admin user established this session.

The value is captured at the moment of successful authentication and typically contains an IPv4 or IPv6 textual representation. It is used heavily for security monitoring, suspicious login detection, and forensic analysis in case of incidents.

href.description:
Full URL accessed when the admin session was created.

This value records the entry point that the admin used when initiating the session, including scheme, host, path, and query string. It helps operators understand which administrative console or route was used at login time and can aid in reconstructing navigation paths.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL reported by the client at the time the session was established.

The referrer provides upstream navigation context such as the page or system from which the admin navigated before logging in. It is stored as a plain string URL and can be used in behavioral analysis or when investigating unusual access flows.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this admin session was created.

This is the moment at which authentication succeeded and the session record was persisted in `todo_app_adminuser_sessions`. It is stored as a non-null datetime in the database and forms the basis for time-based analysis of admin activity, such as listing sessions in reverse chronological order.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when this admin session expired or was terminated.

When the session is still active, this value is null. Once the session ends—either due to explicit logout, timeout, or administrative revocation—the field is populated with the corresponding end-of-life datetime. Downstream tooling can use this to compute session duration and to distinguish active sessions from historical ones when reviewing access windows.

ITodoAppActorSearch.IRequest.description:
Search request payload for querying todoApp actors (guest, member, and admin users).

This schema defines the request body used by the administrative search endpoint that locates different types of user actors across the todoApp domain. It supports filtering by actor classification, identity hints, and lifecycle timestamps and includes pagination and sorting controls.

The intent is to provide a flexible but safe search surface for administrative tooling. It does not expose any authentication secrets and is purely read-only, enabling backoffice and support workflows such as locating a user by email or reviewing recently created accounts.

items.description:
Single actor classification filter value.

Each item restricts the search to one conceptual actor category such as guest, member, or admin. When multiple values are provided, results may contain actors from any of the listed categories.

actorTypes.description:
Set of actor types to include in the search.

When provided, the search is constrained to actors whose underlying Prisma records belong to the specified categories, such as guest users, member users, or admin users. If omitted, the search may consider all actor categories depending on implementation defaults.

email.description:
Optional email filter used when searching member or admin users.

This value is applied to actor types whose underlying Prisma tables carry an `email` column, such as `todo_app_memberusers` and `todo_app_adminusers`. It is ignored for guest users that do not have an email field. Implementations may treat the value as an exact match or a case-insensitive search depending on business rules.

displayName.description:
Optional display name or nickname filter for actors.

The field is intended to match against `display_name` columns in the relevant Prisma tables, such as `todo_app_guestusers.display_name`, `todo_app_memberusers.display_name`, and `todo_app_adminusers.display_name`. It allows administrators to search by human-friendly labels even when precise identifiers like email are not known.

createdFrom.description:
Lower bound of the actor creation timestamp range.

When specified, only actors whose `created_at` value is greater than or equal to this datetime are included in the result set. This supports time-based investigations such as reviewing accounts created after a specific incident date. A null value means no lower bound is applied.

createdTo.description:
Upper bound of the actor creation timestamp range.

When specified, only actors whose `created_at` value is less than or equal to this datetime are included. Combined with `createdFrom`, this supports querying actors created within a given window. A null value means no upper bound is applied.

status.description:
Optional account status filter applied to member and admin users.

The value is compared against the `status` column on `todo_app_memberusers` and `todo_app_adminusers`, which typically encodes states such as active, inactive, disabled, or deleted. For guest users that may not have a status column, this filter is either ignored or mapped according to implementation rules.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated search results.

Administrators use this field to navigate through large result sets. A value of 1 refers to the first page. Implementations should enforce a sensible maximum page value to avoid degenerate queries over very distant pages.

limit.description:
Maximum number of actors to return in a single page.

This field acts as the page size for pagination. Implementations must enforce an upper bound (for example 100 or 200) to protect database performance while still providing efficient browsing of actor records for administrative use.

orderBy.description:
Primary field used to sort the result set.

This enumeration directs the sorting strategy for the search, such as ordering by creation time or by display name. It is applied consistently across actor types so that a single ordering logic can be used even when the underlying Prisma tables differ.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction applied to the chosen orderBy field.

When set to ascending, results are returned from smallest to largest according to the ordering field; when set to descending, the order is reversed. This gives administrators control over whether they see newest, oldest, or alphabetically first actors at the top of the list.

oneOf.description:
Enumeration of conceptual actor categories in the todoApp domain.

This type abstracts over the concrete Prisma models `todo_app_guestusers`, `todo_app_memberusers`, and `todo_app_adminusers` by naming the categories guest, member, and admin. It is used in search and filtering contexts so that administrative APIs can reason about actors without exposing internal table names.

The enumeration values align with the three primary actor roles: guests represent unauthenticated visitors, members represent authenticated end users with personal todo lists, and admins represent privileged operators of the service.

ITodoAppTodo.description:
Todo item entity representing a single task owned by a member user in the todoApp service.

This schema models a row in the todo_app_todos table, which stores core todo data including ownership, content, lifecycle status, and audit timestamps. Each todo belongs to exactly one member user and participates in the todo lifecycle defined by the business requirements.

The todo entity is used as the detailed response shape for create and update operations as well as potential future detail and list endpoints. It exposes only fields that are safe for clients to read while keeping ownership and authentication concerns handled by the backend using relations to the member user entity.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the todo item.

This corresponds to the primary key column id in the todo_app_todos table and is generated by the system as a UUID when the todo is created. Clients receive this value in responses and use it to target specific todos in subsequent operations such as updates or deletions.

memberUser.description:
Owning member user of this todo item.

This object reference represents the row in todo_app_memberusers linked via the todo_app_memberuser_id foreign key. It provides a summary view of the user who owns the todo, allowing clients to display ownership context without exposing authentication details like password hashes.

title.description:
Short textual title of the todo.

This maps to the non-null title column in todo_app_todos and contains the primary label users see in lists. It must be non-empty after trimming and is typically constrained to a reasonable maximum length to ensure good readability.

description.description:
Optional longer description of the todo task.

This corresponds to the nullable description column in todo_app_todos. It may contain additional details or notes entered by the user, or be null when no extra description has been provided.

status.description:
Current business status of the todo.

This is backed by the non-null status column in todo_app_todos. Typical values are "pending" for active items and "completed" for finished tasks, reflecting the lifecycle rules defined in the requirements. Implementation may validate and constrain this field to the allowed status set.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of the todo.

This maps to the created_at column and records when the todo row was first inserted. It is set by the backend at creation time and never decreases. Clients can use it for sorting and display purposes.

updated_at.description:
Last update timestamp of the todo.

This corresponds to the updated_at column in todo_app_todos and is refreshed whenever the todo is modified, including content changes or status transitions. It helps clients track recent activity on the todo.

completed_at.description:
Completion timestamp of the todo.

This field is backed by the nullable completed_at column. It is set when the todo transitions into a completed state and remains null while the todo is pending or has been reopened to active status.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp of the todo.

This maps to the nullable deleted_at column in todo_app_todos. When null, the todo is considered active or completed and appears in normal user listings. When set, the todo is treated as logically deleted and excluded from standard views while remaining available for retention and background cleanup.

ITodoAppTodo.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for querying todo items belonging to the authenticated member user.

This DTO is used as the request body for the `PATCH /todoApp/memberUser/todos` operation and allows clients to express rich filters, sorting options, and pagination controls when retrieving a paginated list of todos from the `todo_app_todos` table.

The filters are applied server-side and are constrained so that a member user can only retrieve their own todos, regardless of any ownership-related criteria specified in this object.

status.description:
Optional exact lifecycle status filter.

When provided, this value limits results to todos whose `status` column in `todo_app_todos` matches the given string (for example, `pending` or `completed`). When null or omitted, todos of all statuses are eligible, subject to other filters.

createdFrom.description:
Optional lower bound for todo creation time.

When set, only todos whose `created_at` timestamp in `todo_app_todos` is greater than or equal to this value are included in the result set. When null or omitted, no lower bound is applied on creation time.

createdTo.description:
Optional upper bound for todo creation time.

When set, only todos whose `created_at` timestamp in `todo_app_todos` is less than or equal to this value are included in the result set. When null or omitted, no upper bound is applied on creation time.

completed.description:
Optional completion state filter.

When true, the search restricts results to todos that are considered completed, typically where `completed_at` in `todo_app_todos` is non-null and the status reflects a completed state. When false, the filter may restrict to todos that are not completed. When null or omitted, completion state is not used as a filter.

search.description:
Optional free-text search term applied to todo content.

This value is used to perform a text-based search across fields such as `title` and, when supported, `description` in `todo_app_todos`. When null or omitted, no free-text search restriction is applied.

page.description:
1-based page index specifying which page of results to return.

This controls pagination over the result set. A value of 1 refers to the first page. Implementation may enforce an upper bound for performance reasons.

limit.description:
Maximum number of todo records to include in a single page of results.

This value determines the page size for the paginated search. The backend enforces an upper limit to prevent excessively large result sets from being returned in a single response.

orderBy.description:
Optional field name used for sorting the result set.

Typical values include `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, or `completedAt`, mapping to corresponding timestamp columns in `todo_app_todos`. When null or omitted, a sensible default order, such as most recently created or updated first, is applied by the service.

orderDirection.description:
Optional sort direction applied together with `orderBy`.

Allowed values are commonly `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. When null or omitted, the backend applies a default direction that matches the primary sort semantics for the chosen `orderBy` field.

ITodoAppTodo.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new todo item for the authenticated member user.

This DTO maps to the todo_app_todos model and collects the business fields that clients are allowed to specify when inserting a new todo row. Ownership information is not exposed in this schema; the backend determines the owning member user from the authenticated context and populates the todo_app_memberuser_id foreign key automatically.

Creation enforces core validation rules such as requiring a non-empty title and using default lifecycle values (for example, setting status to "pending" and timestamps to current time). Fields that are system-managed or derived from the todo lifecycle, such as id and created_at, are intentionally omitted from the request and are filled in by the server.

title.description:
Short textual title of the todo to be created.

This value is persisted to the title column of todo_app_todos and must be non-empty after trimming. The server may enforce a maximum length based on business rules to keep todo lists readable.

description.description:
Optional longer description for the new todo.

When provided, this value is stored in the description column of todo_app_todos. It may be null when the user does not include additional details beyond the title.

ITodoAppTodo.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing todo item belonging to the authenticated member user.

This DTO corresponds to the todo_app_todos model and defines the subset of fields that clients are allowed to change on an existing row. It is used with the update endpoint that targets a specific todo by its UUID path parameter. Ownership and identity fields such as id and the foreign key to the member user are excluded, as they are immutable and managed by the backend.

All properties in this update schema are optional, allowing callers to perform partial updates by including only the fields they wish to change. The backend is responsible for enforcing lifecycle consistency when status-related fields are updated and for refreshing the updated_at timestamp on each successful modification.

title.description:
New title for the todo, if it is being changed.

When present, this value replaces the existing title in the todo_app_todos row. It must remain non-empty after trimming and respect any configured maximum length constraints.

description.description:
Updated description for the todo, if it is being modified.

Providing a non-null string replaces the existing description with new content. Supplying null clears the description, making the column effectively empty.

status.description:
Updated lifecycle status of the todo.

This value updates the status column in todo_app_todos. Typical values include "pending" and "completed". When changing status, the service may also adjust related timestamp fields such as completed_at according to the lifecycle rules.

ITodoAppTodoStatusSummary.description:
Aggregated status summary for todo items owned by the currently authenticated member user.

This DTO is a computed, read-only analytical view derived from the todo_app_todos model. It summarizes the member user's todos by business status (such as pending and completed) and exposes counters and simple derived metrics used for dashboard widgets and status overviews.

The structure intentionally avoids exposing individual todo rows or any identifying information beyond aggregate counts, ensuring minimal payload size and strong privacy guarantees while still allowing clients to understand their workload at a glance.

total_count.description:
Total number of non-deleted todos owned by the current member user.

This count is computed from todo_app_todos rows filtered by the authenticated member user's id and excluding logically deleted items (for example, rows with deleted_at set). It includes both pending and completed tasks so that clients can display the overall number of todos managed by the user.

pending_count.description:
Number of active/pending todos for the current member user.

This value is derived from todo_app_todos where the status field represents an active or pending state (for example, status = "pending") and deleted_at is null. It is used by clients to show how many tasks remain to be completed.

completed_count.description:
Number of completed todos for the current member user.

This count is computed from todo_app_todos rows whose status field represents a completed state (for example, status = "completed") and that are still visible according to logical deletion rules. It allows clients to indicate how many tasks have been finished.

recently_completed_count.description:
Number of todos recently completed by the current member user.

This optional metric is derived by constraining todo_app_todos rows to those with a non-null completed_at timestamp falling within a recent time window such as the last day or week, while still respecting logical deletion. It enables UI elements like "completed today" or "recently finished" badges without requiring clients to perform their own date-based aggregations.

ITodoAppLoginAttempt.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for querying login attempt records from the todo_app_login_attempts table.

This DTO represents the structured request body accepted by the administrative login-attempt search API. It allows privileged admin users to filter historical authentication attempts based on identifiers, actor type, success flag, time range, and network context, as well as control pagination settings.

The parameters map directly onto the fields and indexes of the todo_app_login_attempts model (including login_identifier, actor_type, succeeded, ip, failure_reason, and created_at) so that the backend can efficiently build queries for operational security dashboards and incident investigation tools. All fields are optional so that administrators can start with broad views and incrementally refine their searches.

page.description:
Page index for paginated results.

Represents the 1-based page number to retrieve when listing login attempts. If omitted, the backend may default to the first page. Used together with limit to implement cursorless, offset-based pagination over the todo_app_login_attempts result set.

limit.description:
Maximum number of login attempt rows to return in a single page.

Controls the page size for the login-attempt search results. Typical values are bounded to a reasonable range (for example, 20–100) to protect the system from excessively large responses and to work well with the indexes defined on todo_app_login_attempts.

login_identifier.description:
Login identifier used in attempted authentication, such as an email address or username.

Filters login attempts by the normalized identifier stored in todo_app_login_attempts.login_identifier. Administrators can use this to inspect all attempts made against a specific account name or email, regardless of whether the attempts succeeded.

actor_type.description:
