High-level actor type that attempted to authenticate.

Corresponds to the actor_type column of todo_app_login_attempts, which distinguishes between different logical actor categories such as guestUser, memberUser, or adminUser. When supplied, only attempts whose actor_type matches the provided value are returned.

succeeded.description:
Filter flag indicating whether to return only successful or only failed login attempts.

When true, only rows where todo_app_login_attempts.succeeded is true are included, representing successful authentications. When false, only failed attempts are included. If omitted, both successful and failed attempts may be returned according to the backend's default behavior.

ip.description:
Client IP address from which login attempts originated.

Filters login attempts by the ip column of todo_app_login_attempts. This is typically an IPv4 or IPv6 string captured at the edge and is used by administrators to investigate suspicious activity from particular network sources.

failure_reason.description:
High-level reason code for failed login attempts.

Corresponds to the failure_reason column in todo_app_login_attempts, which may contain values such as invalid_credentials, account_locked, or rate_limited. When provided, only failed attempts with the matching reason are returned; successful attempts are usually excluded from this filter.

created_from.description:
Start of the created_at time window for the query, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

When set to a non-null value, only login attempts whose created_at timestamp is greater than or equal to this value are included. This allows administrators to constrain searches to recent activity or to a specific incident window.

created_to.description:
End of the created_at time window for the query, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

When set to a non-null value, only login attempts whose created_at timestamp is less than or equal to this value are included. Combined with created_from, this enables precise time-bounded log reviews.

ITodoAppLoginAttempt.description:
Represents a single authentication attempt recorded in the todo_app_login_attempts Prisma table.

This entity captures both successful and failed login attempts for member and admin users, including the login identifier used, actor classification, outcome, and contextual metadata such as IP address and user agent.

It is used exclusively for security auditing, rate limiting analysis, and incident investigation workflows and does not participate directly in the business lifecycle of todos.

Login attempt records are immutable once written and serve as an operational audit trail for the authentication layer. They are queried by administrative endpoints to monitor abuse, validate that lockout and rate limiting rules are behaving as expected, and correlate events across member users, admin users, and IP ranges.

The underlying data is stored in the `todo_app_login_attempts` Prisma model, which also maintains nullable foreign keys to `todo_app_memberusers` and `todo_app_adminusers`. This DTO surfaces those relationships through compact `memberUser` and `adminUser` summaries instead of exposing raw foreign key identifiers directly.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the login attempt record.

This is the primary key of the corresponding row in the todo_app_login_attempts table and is used to retrieve a specific attempt entry for security auditing or investigation.

Clients should treat this value as an opaque identifier that is stable over the lifetime of the record.

login_identifier.description:
Login identifier provided by the client when attempting authentication.

Typically this is an email-style value or username as supplied by the user. It is stored after any normalization rules so that repeated failures can be correlated reliably during abuse detection and rate limiting.

Security dashboards often group or filter login attempts by this value to understand which identifiers are being targeted over time.

actor_type.description:
High-level classification of the actor that attempted the login.

Common values include guestUser, memberUser, and adminUser. The value is determined by authentication logic based on the identifier and system configuration so that downstream security tools can distinguish end-user activity from administrative access patterns.

This field is particularly useful when aggregating statistics or building visualizations that separate regular user traffic from privileged administrator access attempts.

succeeded.description:
Indicates whether this login attempt successfully resulted in an authenticated session.

A value of true means credential validation passed and a session was established; false indicates invalid credentials, blocked accounts, or other authentication failures as captured in the failure_reason field.

Operations teams can use this flag to quickly distinguish normal usage from repeated failure patterns that may indicate credential stuffing or brute-force attacks.

ip.description:
IP address from which the login attempt originated.

This value is captured at the time of the request and is used for rate limiting windows, geolocation-based security checks, and forensic analysis during incident response.

Depending on deployment topology, this may represent a client IP, proxy, or edge gateway address; system documentation should clarify how forwarded-for headers are handled when interpreting this value.

user_agent.description:
User agent string reported by the client for this login attempt.

The value may be null when the client does not provide a user agent. When present, it helps identify automated scripts, unusual clients, and device or browser characteristics relevant to security investigations.

Security tooling can use this field in combination with IP and actor_type to spot suspicious patterns, such as the same script attacking multiple accounts from a shared network range.

failure_reason.description:
High-level category describing why the login failed, if applicable.

Typical values include invalid_credentials, account_locked, or rate_limited. The value is null when succeeded is true. This field enables security and operations staff to quickly understand failure modes without parsing low-level log messages.

The exact taxonomy of failure reason codes is defined by the authentication service and should remain stable enough to support dashboards and alerting rules.

memberUser.description:
Optional summary of the member user whose account was targeted by this login attempt.

When present, this field corresponds to the member account referenced by the underlying todo_app_memberuser_id foreign key in the todo_app_login_attempts table. It exposes a lightweight summary view of the member, such as identifier and display name, instead of the raw UUID.

The value is omitted or null when the login identifier did not match any member user at the time of the attempt or when the attempt is associated with a different actor type.

adminUser.description:
Optional summary of the admin user whose account was targeted by this login attempt.

When present, this field corresponds to the admin account referenced by the underlying todo_app_adminuser_id foreign key in the todo_app_login_attempts table. It surfaces a compact administrative user summary suitable for security dashboards instead of a bare UUID.

The value is omitted or null when the login identifier did not match any admin user at the time of the attempt or when the attempt relates to another actor type.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this login attempt was recorded.

Stored in the database as a DateTime column, it defines the temporal position of the event, supports rate limiting windows, and provides the primary time axis for security audit queries.

Clients should expect an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC and can use this value to construct time-series charts or to restrict investigations to a specific incident window.

ITodoAppAdminTodoAction.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for querying administrative actions on todo items stored in the todo_app_admin_todo_actions audit log.

This DTO is used by the PATCH /todoApp/adminUser/adminTodoActions endpoint to express flexible search criteria, pagination controls, and sorting preferences when retrieving admin interventions for security monitoring, compliance reporting, and operational review.

All properties are optional filters or controls. When omitted, the implementation should return a sensible default view such as the most recent actions ordered by created_at in descending order.

page.description:
Page number to retrieve in a page-based pagination model.

Clients should start from 1 for the first page. When omitted, the implementation may default to the first page. Combined with pageSize it determines which window of audit records is returned.

pageSize.description:
Maximum number of admin todo action records to return in a single page.

Used together with page to implement offset-based pagination. Implementations should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large responses.

adminUserId.description:
Optional filter restricting results to actions performed by a specific admin user.

When provided, only records whose todo_app_adminuser_id matches this identifier are included. The UUID corresponds to todo_app_adminusers.id.

memberUserId.description:
Optional filter restricting results to actions that targeted todos belonging to a specific member user.

When provided, only records whose todo_app_memberuser_id matches this identifier are returned. The UUID corresponds to todo_app_memberusers.id.

todoId.description:
Optional filter restricting results to actions performed on a single todo item.

When provided, only records whose todo_app_todo_id matches this identifier are included. The UUID corresponds to todo_app_todos.id.

actionType.description:
Optional filter for the high-level type of administrative action taken on the todo.

Examples include delete_todo, hide_todo, or neutralize_content. When provided, only audit records with the matching action_type value are returned.

reasonCategory.description:
Optional filter for the high-level reason category that justified the administrative action.

Typical values include policy_violation, legal_request, abuse_report, or operational_cleanup. When specified, only actions with the matching reason_category are included.

occurredFrom.description:
Optional lower bound for the action timestamp range to search.

When provided, only admin todo actions with created_at greater than or equal to this timestamp are returned. This is typically used together with occurredTo to bound a time window.

occurredTo.description:
Optional upper bound for the action timestamp range to search.

When provided, only admin todo actions with created_at less than or equal to this timestamp are included. Together with occurredFrom it defines a closed time interval for the query.

sortBy.description:
Field used to sort the resulting admin todo action records.

Typical values include created_at or action_type. When omitted, implementations should default to a sensible field such as created_at.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction for the result ordering.

Expected values are asc for ascending or desc for descending order. When omitted, implementations usually default to desc to show most recent actions first.

ITodoAppAdminTodoAction.description:
Detailed audit log entry representing a single administrative action performed on a member user's todo item.

This type maps directly to the `todo_app_admin_todo_actions` Prisma model and is used as the full detail view returned from the admin audit read API. It exposes the core identifying fields of the audit record, the high-level classification of the action and its reason, the involved actors and target todo, and the timestamp of when the action was recorded.

The structure is designed for administrative and security oversight workflows. It enables compliance teams, security operators, and support staff to reconstruct who changed what, when, and for which conceptual reason, without exposing any password or authentication secret fields.

Relations to `todo_app_adminusers`, `todo_app_memberusers`, and `todo_app_todos` are represented through summary DTO references so that the inspector can see the involved admin account, the affected member account, and the target todo at a glance while avoiding circular expansion of related entities.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this admin todo action audit record.

This field maps to the primary key column of the `todo_app_admin_todo_actions` table and is generated by the system when the audit entry is created. It is used as the stable identifier for lookups through admin audit APIs and in internal tooling.

Clients receive this value in read responses only; it is never provided by callers in request bodies.

adminUser.description:
Summary information for the administrative user who performed this action.

This reference corresponds to the `todo_app_adminuser_id` foreign key in the `todo_app_admin_todo_actions` Prisma model. It provides enough detail about the operator account for audit and accountability purposes without expanding to all admin-related aggregates.

The summary variant prevents circular references while still allowing reviewers to recognize which admin account initiated the action.

memberUser.description:
Summary information for the member user who owns the affected todo item.

This reference corresponds to the `todo_app_memberuser_id` foreign key in the `todo_app_admin_todo_actions` table. It lets auditors understand which end-user account was impacted by the administrative intervention.

Only non-sensitive profile and identification fields should be exposed here, following the summary DTO convention for member users.

todo.description:
Summary of the todo item that the admin acted upon.

This reference is derived from the `todo_app_todo_id` foreign key in the `todo_app_admin_todo_actions` Prisma model. It provides minimal context about the target todo, such as its title and current state, without returning the entire todo detail.

Using the summary variant allows admin consoles to show what item was changed while maintaining good performance and avoiding deep nested structures.

action_type.description:
High-level type of administrative action that was applied to the todo item.

The value originates from the `action_type` column of the `todo_app_admin_todo_actions` table. Typical examples include values such as `delete_todo`, `hide_todo`, `force_complete`, `restore_todo`, or similar operation codes defined by policy.

Downstream reporting and analytics tools use this field to group actions by category, enabling dashboards that summarize moderation activity or operational cleanup events.

reason_category.description:
Categorized reason explaining why this administrative action was taken.

This field maps to the `reason_category` column of the `todo_app_admin_todo_actions` Prisma model. Example values may include `policy_violation`, `legal_request`, `abuse_report`, or `operational_cleanup`, depending on how the service classifies interventions.

Operators and compliance reviewers use this category to quickly filter and analyze actions based on high-level business or regulatory motivations, without reading the full free-form description.

reason_detail.description:
Optional free-form explanatory text that provides additional context about the action.

This property is backed by the `reason_detail` column of the `todo_app_admin_todo_actions` table and may be null when no extra explanation was recorded. When present, it can contain internal notes written by the admin or structured details generated by the system.

The content should be treated as potentially sensitive operational data and is intended primarily for internal use. It should avoid including unnecessary personal information while still giving reviewers enough information to understand the context of the decision.

ip.description:
Optional IP address from which the admin performed this action.

This value corresponds to the `ip` column in the `todo_app_admin_todo_actions` Prisma model. It may be null when the system cannot reliably capture the source IP or when policy forbids storing it.

When present, it supports security investigations and anomaly detection by allowing correlation of admin actions with network origin patterns. Implementations should treat it as sensitive operational data and handle it according to privacy requirements.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this administrative action was recorded in the audit log.

This field maps directly to the `created_at` column of the `todo_app_admin_todo_actions` table. It reflects the moment the backend wrote the audit entry, which typically matches closely when the underlying moderation action took effect.

Audit tooling and reporting features use this timestamp for chronological ordering, time-based filtering, and correlation with user-visible changes in the todo lifecycle.

ITodoAppTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a todo item owned by a member user.

This type is designed for list views, search results, and lightweight embeddings where showing the entire todo record is unnecessary. It focuses on the most important fields that describe the todo at a glance, such as title, status, and key timestamps.

The summary representation intentionally omits the full description body and any heavy composition relations, but it still includes a minimal owner context via the member user summary so that administrative tools can understand which account the item belongs to.

Clients typically obtain this type from list endpoints that page through todos, and use the todo identifier to navigate to a detailed view when the user opens a specific item.

id.description:
Primary key of the todo item.

This value is the `id` column from `todo_app_todos` and uniquely identifies a single todo across the system.

Clients use this identifier when requesting detailed views or when performing operations that target a specific todo, such as update or delete.

title.description:
Short textual title of the todo.

Directly reflects the `title` column in `todo_app_todos`. The value is required, non-empty after trimming, and constrained to a reasonable maximum length to keep list presentations readable.

This is the primary piece of text shown in todo lists and search results.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the todo.

This field corresponds to the `status` column in `todo_app_todos` and usually takes values such as `pending` for active items or `completed` for finished tasks, in alignment with the lifecycle rules defined for the service.

List endpoints can filter or group todos by this status, and UIs can render different visual styles based on the current state.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of the todo item.

This value is taken from the `created_at` column of `todo_app_todos` and represents when the todo was originally recorded by the system.

Summaries often use this field for chronological sorting or for showing when the todo first appeared in the user’s list.

updated_at.description:
Latest modification timestamp of the todo item.

This corresponds to the `updated_at` column in `todo_app_todos` and is updated whenever the todo’s content or status changes.

Clients can use this field to highlight recently edited items or to detect when cached list entries may be stale.

completed_at.description:
Completion timestamp of the todo when it is in the completed state.

The value is taken from the `completed_at` column of `todo_app_todos`. It is null while the todo is still pending or when a previously completed item has been reopened as active.

This field allows lists to show when tasks were finished and to provide filters based on completion recency.

memberUser.description:
Summary information about the member user who owns this todo.

This object is derived from `todo_app_memberusers` and provides a minimal view of the owning account, such as identifier, display name, and optional email for administrative contexts.

Including this summary in todo lists is especially useful for administrative tools that need to see at a glance which user each todo belongs to without making additional queries.

ITodoAppRateLimitEvent.IRequest.description:
Request payload used by administrators to search and paginate through rate limit events recorded by the todoApp backend.

This DTO encapsulates filter criteria and pagination settings that are translated into queries against the `todo_app_rate_limit_events` Prisma model. It allows operators to narrow results by time windows, actor type, client identifiers such as IP address, and the logical rate limit key and category.

The structure is intentionally flexible and should be extended in alignment with the underlying Prisma schema and operational monitoring requirements, while still enforcing reasonable defaults and bounds on pagination-related values.

actor_type.description:
Optional filter on the actor type that triggered the rate limit event.

Typical values match those stored in the `actor_type` column of the `todo_app_rate_limit_events` table, such as `guestUser`, `memberUser`, or `adminUser`. When provided, only events associated with the specified actor classification are returned.

When null or omitted, the search is not constrained by actor type and will include events for all actor classifications.

ip.description:
Optional filter on the client IP address associated with rate limited requests.

This corresponds conceptually to the `ip` column of the `todo_app_rate_limit_events` schema. When set, the query engine restricts results to events recorded for the given IP address.

If null or not provided, events across all IPs are considered, which is useful for global audits but may be more expensive for large datasets.

limit_key.description:
Optional filter on the logical rate limiting key that was enforced.

The value should match entries stored in the `limit_key` column of `todo_app_rate_limit_events`, such as `login_identifier`, `account_id`, `ip`, or application-specific endpoint group identifiers. Filtering by this field allows operators to investigate a particular rate limit rule.

When null or omitted, the search covers all limit keys defined in the system.

limit_type.description:
Optional filter that narrows results to a specific rate limit category.

This parameter is aligned with the `limit_type` column in the `todo_app_rate_limit_events` table and may contain values like `auth_login`, `todo_write`, `admin_action`, or `global_client_limit` depending on how the backend classifies limits.

If absent or null, events of all limit categories are eligible to be returned in the search results.

window_start_from.description:
Lower bound of the rate limit window start time to include in the search.

When provided, only events whose `window_start` is greater than or equal to this timestamp are returned. This allows administrators to focus on recent rate limiting behavior or investigate a specific incident period.

If null or omitted, no explicit lower bound on the window start is applied beyond any global retention constraints of the underlying table.

window_start_to.description:
Upper bound of the rate limit window start time to include in the search.

When set, only events whose `window_start` is less than or equal to this timestamp are considered. Combined with `window_start_from`, this supports querying events within a specific time interval.

If null or not provided, there is no explicit upper bound on `window_start`, and the query can return the most recent events available.

page.description:
1-based index of the result page to retrieve.

This parameter controls which slice of the overall result set is returned. A value of 1 corresponds to the first page. Implementations should clamp values below 1 to 1 or return a validation error based on service policy.

If not provided, backends typically default this to 1 to return the first page of results.

pageSize.description:
Maximum number of rate limit event records to include in a single page of results.

This value determines the size of the `data` array in the paginated response. Implementations should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large pages that could degrade performance, for example limiting this to 100 or 200 entries.

If omitted, a sensible default page size such as 20 or 50 should be applied by the server.

sort_by.description:
Optional field name used to sort rate limit events in the result set.

Commonly supported values would include `created_at`, `window_start`, or `limit_key`, matching columns in the `todo_app_rate_limit_events` table. If unsupported values are supplied, the server should return a validation error describing allowed options.

When null or absent, the default sort order is typically descending by `created_at` or another time-based field so that recent events appear first.

sort_order.description:
Optional sort direction applied to the chosen `sort_by` field.

Typical accepted values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending ordering. When provided together with `sort_by`, this property guides how the backend orders the results within each page.

If null or missing, the service should default to a sensible direction, commonly `desc` when sorting by time-based fields like `created_at` or `window_start`.

ITodoAppRateLimitEvent.description:
Represents a single rate limit enforcement event recorded by the todoApp service.

Each record corresponds to one instance where a configured rate limit was exceeded for some actor context, logical limit key, or IP address. It captures both the categorization of the limit and the exact time window during which throttling is applied.

This DTO is used in administrative and security-observability APIs to inspect when and why a client or user was rate limited. It mirrors the todo_app_rate_limit_events Prisma model and is strictly read-only from an API perspective.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this rate limit event.

This value is the primary key of the corresponding row in the todo_app_rate_limit_events table and is used as the stable reference in administrative APIs such as GET /todoApp/adminUser/rateLimitEvents/{rateLimitEventId}.

It is generated by the system when the rate limiting subsystem records an event and is immutable thereafter.

actor_type.description:
Actor category that triggered this rate limit event.

Typical values describe the high-level role of the requester such as guestUser, memberUser, or adminUser. This allows operators to differentiate rate limiting behavior between anonymous traffic, authenticated members, and administrative users.

Although modeled as a free-form string at the database level, the service should constrain values to a small set of known actor types for consistent analysis.

oneOf.description:
IP address to which this rate limit event applies.

When present, this stores the client IP address that exceeded a configured rate limit. It is commonly used for anonymous or guest-based throttling where no authenticated user account is available.

The value should be a textual IPv4 or IPv6 representation as captured by the edge or API gateway.

No IP address associated with this rate limit event.

Null indicates that the limit evaluation did not bind to a specific IP address, for example when the limit is keyed only by user account or some other logical key.

ip.description:
Optional IP address context for this rate limit event.

When non-null, this value identifies the client IP that was evaluated by the rate limiting subsystem. When null, the limit was applied without binding to a specific IP address, such as purely account-based or key-based limits.

limit_key.description:
Logical key used by the rate limiting subsystem when evaluating this request.

Examples include login_identifier, account_id, ip, or an endpoint-group identifier. The value groups requests into a bucket whose activity is measured against the configured threshold.

Operators can use this field to correlate multiple events that share the same limiting dimension and to tune rate limit policies over time.

limit_type.description:
Category of rate limit that was exceeded for this event.

Typical values describe the high-level purpose of the limit, such as auth_login, todo_write, admin_action, or global_client_limit. This categorization allows monitoring dashboards to distinguish between different protection layers.

The concrete set of limit types is controlled by the rate limiting configuration and should remain stable for consistent analysis.

window_start.description:
Start timestamp of the enforcement window for this rate limit event.

This marks the beginning of the interval over which the request volume was evaluated and after which throttling is applied to the offending client, user, or key.

Combined with window_end, it describes the time range during which further requests may be rejected or delayed.

window_end.description:
End timestamp of the enforcement window for this rate limit event.

Until this time, requests associated with the same limit_key and actor context may continue to experience throttling in accordance with the configured policy.

After window_end, the rate limiting subsystem will typically allow traffic to resume normal behavior for this key, subject to new evaluations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this rate limit event record was persisted.

This value reflects when the system detected the threshold breach and wrote the corresponding log entry to the todo_app_rate_limit_events table.

It is useful for ordering events chronologically and correlating them with application request logs or security monitoring data.

oneOf.description:
Summary representation of the member user associated with this rate limit event.

When present, this contains a lightweight view of the `todo_app_memberusers` row that owned the request context in which the rate limit was enforced. It is intended for administrative observability and correlation in dashboards and tooling, not for direct identity management.

To inspect or manage the member account in detail, use the dedicated member user administration APIs that return the full `ITodoAppMemberUser` DTO.

No member user associated with this rate limit event.

Null indicates that the rate limiting decision was not tied to an authenticated member account, for example when the actor was a guest user or an administrative user.

member_user.description:
Optional summary of the member user related to this rate limit event.

This association is included for context so that administrators can quickly see which member account was impacted by rate limiting. It follows the standard association pattern by using the `ITodoAppMemberUser.ISummary` DTO to avoid circular references and keep the payload compact.

oneOf.description:
Summary representation of the admin user associated with this rate limit event.

When present, this contains a lightweight view of the `todo_app_adminusers` row whose actions or requests triggered the rate limit. It is used for security auditing and operational analysis rather than for direct admin account management.

For full administrative user details, consumers should call the appropriate admin user inspection endpoints that return `ITodoAppAdminUser` or related DTOs.

No admin user associated with this rate limit event.

Null indicates that the rate limit was applied in a non-admin context, such as member or guest traffic, or in a purely key-based scenario with no bound admin account.

admin_user.description:
Optional summary of the admin user related to this rate limit event.

This association helps administrators and security operators understand which administrative account, if any, was impacted by the rate limiting rule. It uses the `ITodoAppAdminUser.ISummary` schema to provide just enough context without introducing heavy nesting or circular references.

ITodoAppMemberuserSession.ISummary.description:
Compact summary view of an authentication session for a todoApp member user.

This summary type is used in list APIs and embedded contexts where a quick overview of recent or active sessions is required, without loading full user or request details.

It captures only the identifying information, key connection context, and temporal fields necessary to audit session lifetime and origin. Ownership of the session by a specific member user is provided by the surrounding API context (for example, the `memberUserId` path parameter) rather than by an explicit foreign key property.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the member user session.

This maps to the primary key of the `todo_app_memberuser_sessions` table and is used to reference a specific login session in logs or management operations.

ip.description:
IP address from which the member user established this session.

Stored in textual form and typically representing either an IPv4 or IPv6 address, this field is essential for security monitoring and anomaly detection workflows.

href.description:
Full URL that the user was visiting when the session was created.

This captures the entry point into the application, including path and query string, and is useful for understanding how users initiate authentication flows.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL reported by the client at the moment the session was established.

It helps reconstruct navigation flows into the service, such as which external page or internal screen led to the login attempt.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this session record was created.

Represents the moment when authentication succeeded and the session became valid. Used for sorting and analyzing login activity over time.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when this session was invalidated or naturally expired.

When null, the session is considered currently active according to the persistence layer, although application logic may apply additional real‑time checks or token validations.

ITodoAppActorSearch.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an actor result in the todoApp actor search feature.

This type is returned when searching for actors (member users, admin users, or guest users) so that the client can display a unified, lightweight card for each matching identity.

It intentionally exposes only non-sensitive, non-authentication profile data and a small amount of contextual information useful for search result lists, while omitting any credential or security-related fields.

The summary result includes the actor type discriminator, a stable identifier, and basic display information such as display name and email when applicable, plus optional last-activity timestamps used for ordering and hinting recency.

Search consumers can inspect the actorType field to decide which follow-up detail API to call for the specific actor domain (member user, admin user, or guest user).

oneOf.description:
High-level type of the actor returned by search.

Typical values are "guestUser" for unauthenticated identities, "memberUser" for regular authenticated users, and "adminUser" for administrative operators.

The client inspects this value to determine how to render the actor and which detail endpoint to call for more information.

High-level type of the actor returned by search.

Typical values are "guestUser" for unauthenticated identities, "memberUser" for regular authenticated users, and "adminUser" for administrative operators.

The client inspects this value to determine how to render the actor and which detail endpoint to call for more information.

High-level type of the actor returned by search.

Typical values are "guestUser" for unauthenticated identities, "memberUser" for regular authenticated users, and "adminUser" for administrative operators.

The client inspects this value to determine how to render the actor and which detail endpoint to call for more information.

actorType.description:
High-level type of the actor returned by search.

Typical values are "guestUser" for unauthenticated identities, "memberUser" for regular authenticated users, and "adminUser" for administrative operators.

The client inspects this value to determine how to render the actor and which detail endpoint to call for more information.

id.description:
Primary identifier of the actor within its own domain.

For member users this matches `todo_app_memberusers.id`, for admin users `todo_app_adminusers.id`, and for guest users `todo_app_guestusers.id`.

The combination of `actorType` and this `id` uniquely identifies an actor across the entire todoApp service.

display_name.description:
Human-friendly display name of the actor when available.

For member and admin users this is the `display_name` column from their respective tables. For guest users this is the optional `display_name` from `todo_app_guestusers`.

When not set in the database, the field may be an empty string or omitted from the payload; clients should gracefully handle missing or blank values.

email.description:
Email-style login identifier for the actor when applicable.

For member and admin users this corresponds to the `email` column of their account table. Guest users do not have an email stored and therefore this field is omitted for them.

This value is provided only for display in administrative or self-account search contexts and must not be treated as a credential or token.

status.description:
Account status for the actor when applicable.

For member and admin users this reflects the `status` column of their respective tables, such as `active`, `inactive`, or `disabled`. Guest users do not have an account status; this field is omitted for them.

Search interfaces can use this value to gray out disabled accounts or to filter interactive actions that are not allowed for non-active actors.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the actor’s most recent successful login when relevant.

For member and admin users this value comes from the `last_login_at` column of their account record. For guest users, or for actors that have never logged in successfully, the value is null and may be omitted from the payload.

This field helps sort or annotate search results by recent activity without exposing any sensitive session details.

ITodoAppLoginAttempt.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for todoApp login attempt records used in list views, security dashboards, and rate‑limit audit screens.

This summary focuses on the core identifying and classification fields that are most useful when scanning lists of attempts, such as who tried to log in, from where, and whether the attempt succeeded. It omits large or rarely used fields and retains only concise contextual information.

The underlying data is stored in the `todo_app_login_attempts` Prisma model, which tracks both successful and failed authentication attempts, including IP address and optional user agent for security analysis and abuse detection.

This summary type is typically returned by search or reporting endpoints that paginate through many login attempts, rather than detailed single‑attempt inspection endpoints.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the login attempt record.

This value maps directly to `todo_app_login_attempts.id` and is used as the primary key when referencing a specific attempt in logs, links, or administrative tools.

Clients generally treat this as an opaque value used only for identification and not for any business logic.

login_identifier.description:
Login identifier supplied by the client, such as normalized email or username.

This field comes from `todo_app_login_attempts.login_identifier` and is stored as received after any normalization rules. It enables operators to see which identifier is being targeted by repeated attempts and to correlate patterns of abuse across time.

When rendered in UIs, this value should be handled carefully to avoid leaking sensitive identifiers to unauthorized viewers.

actor_type.description:
High‑level actor type that attempted the login.

This value reflects `todo_app_login_attempts.actor_type` and is typically one of `guestUser`, `memberUser`, or `adminUser`, depending on how the authentication logic classified the attempt.

Security tools can use this field to filter or group attempts by user category, for example to focus on member logins versus administrative access attempts.

succeeded.description:
Indicates whether this login attempt successfully created an authenticated session.

This field maps to `todo_app_login_attempts.succeeded`. A value of `true` represents valid credentials and non‑blocked account state at the time of the attempt, while `false` represents failures such as invalid credentials, blocked accounts, or rate‑limited requests.

Operators often use this flag to quickly distinguish normal usage from repeated failure patterns that may indicate credential stuffing or brute‑force attacks.

ip.description:
IP address from which the login attempt originated.

This value comes from `todo_app_login_attempts.ip` and is captured at the time of the request. It supports rate‑limiting enforcement, geo‑based analysis, and incident investigations when unusual login activity is detected.

Depending on deployment, the IP may represent the client, a proxy, or an edge gateway; network topology and `X‑Forwarded‑For` handling must be considered when interpreting this value.

failure_reason.description:
Optional high‑level category describing why the login failed.

This field reflects `todo_app_login_attempts.failure_reason`. Typical values include categories such as `invalid_credentials`, `account_locked`, or `rate_limited`, but the exact taxonomy is defined by the authentication service.

The value is `null` for successful attempts where there is no failure reason to record. Consumers should treat this as descriptive metadata for security analysis rather than a user‑facing error message.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the login attempt was recorded.

This property is backed by `todo_app_login_attempts.created_at` and uses an ISO 8601 date‑time string in UTC. It enables chronological sorting, time‑window based rate‑limiting checks, and correlation with other security events.

Reporting tools often use this field to group attempts by hour or day and to visualize spikes in authentication activity.

memberUser.description:
Optional summary of the member user account associated with this login attempt.

When present, this summary corresponds to the member account that the underlying `todo_app_memberuser_id` foreign key points to in `todo_app_login_attempts`. It provides a compact view of the targeted member for list and dashboard presentations without exposing a raw UUID.

The field is omitted or null when no member account was matched for the login identifier or when the attempt pertains to a different actor type.

adminUser.description:
Optional summary of the administrative user account associated with this login attempt.

When present, this summary corresponds to the admin account that the underlying `todo_app_adminuser_id` foreign key refers to in `todo_app_login_attempts`. It supplies condensed admin context in list responses instead of a bare UUID.

The field is omitted or null when no admin account was matched for the login identifier or when the attempt does not involve an admin actor.

ITodoAppAdminTodoAction.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for administrative actions performed on todo items in the todoApp service.

This summary focuses on the key identifiers and categorization fields needed to review how administrators have interacted with member todos, such as which todo was affected, which admin acted, what type of action was taken, and why.

The data is stored in the `todo_app_admin_todo_actions` Prisma model as an append‑only audit log. Each record links an admin user, a member user, and a todo item, along with action metadata and the creation timestamp.

This summary type is typically used by audit dashboards, compliance tools, and support consoles that paginate through many administrative interventions rather than inspecting a single event in exhaustive detail.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the administrative todo action record.

This value maps directly to `todo_app_admin_todo_actions.id` and acts as the primary key for referencing a specific admin intervention in logs, links, or internal tools.

Clients treat this as an opaque identifier that is stable over time and suitable for bookmarking or deep‑linking into audit detail views.

adminUser.description:
Summary information for the administrative user who performed this action.

This reference corresponds to the `todo_app_adminuser_id` foreign key in the `todo_app_admin_todo_actions` Prisma model. It provides enough detail about the operator account for audit and accountability purposes without expanding to all admin-related aggregates.

The summary variant prevents circular references while still allowing reviewers to recognize which admin account initiated the action.

memberUser.description:
Summary information for the member user who owns the affected todo item.

This reference corresponds to the `todo_app_memberuser_id` foreign key in the `todo_app_admin_todo_actions` table. It lets auditors understand which end-user account was impacted by the administrative intervention.

Only non-sensitive profile and identification fields should be exposed here, following the summary DTO convention for member users.

todo.description:
Summary of the todo item that the admin acted upon.

This reference is derived from the `todo_app_todo_id` foreign key in the `todo_app_admin_todo_actions` Prisma model. It provides minimal context about the target todo, such as its title and current state, without returning the entire todo detail.

Using the summary variant allows admin consoles to show what item was changed while maintaining good performance and avoiding deep nested structures.

action_type.description:
High‑level type of administrative action applied to the todo item.

The value is stored in `todo_app_admin_todo_actions.action_type` and typically follows a constrained vocabulary such as `delete_todo`, `hide_todo`, or `neutralize_content`, but the exact set of codes is defined by product policy.

This category enables grouping and filtering of admin actions for reporting, for example to measure how many todos were removed for policy violations versus routine clean‑up.

reason_category.description:
High‑level reason code explaining why this administrative action was taken.

This property corresponds to `todo_app_admin_todo_actions.reason_category`. Example values include `policy_violation`, `legal_request`, `abuse_report`, or `operational_cleanup`, though the concrete taxonomy is defined by service governance.

Security and compliance teams rely on this field to analyze patterns in moderation decisions and to ensure consistent application of policy.

reason_detail.description:
Optional free‑form description with additional context about the action.

The text originates from `todo_app_admin_todo_actions.reason_detail` and may be written by the acting admin or generated by the system. It can capture nuanced explanations that do not fit into a simple reason code.

Because this field can contain sensitive or potentially identifying information, client applications should enforce appropriate access control and avoid exposing it broadly without need.

ip.description:
Optional IP address from which the administrative action was performed.

This value maps to `todo_app_admin_todo_actions.ip`. When present, it helps security teams review whether actions originated from expected admin networks, VPNs, or devices.

The field is nullable because some environments may not capture admin IP data, or actions may be triggered by internal batch processes where no meaningful client IP exists.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the administrative action was recorded.

This value comes from `todo_app_admin_todo_actions.created_at` and uses an ISO 8601 UTC date‑time string. It provides chronological ordering and supports correlation with member‑visible effects, such as when a todo disappeared from a user’s list.

Audit and reporting tools typically sort by this field and may also aggregate actions into hourly or daily buckets for monitoring trends.

ITodoAppRateLimitEvent.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a rate limit enforcement event in the todoApp service.

This DTO is designed for lightweight listing, monitoring dashboards, and log inspection screens where operators or automated systems need to understand when and why a rate limit was triggered without loading full relational context.

It maps directly onto the `todo_app_rate_limit_events` Prisma model and only exposes non-sensitive operational fields. Relationships to member and admin users are not expanded into nested objects in this summary representation, keeping payloads compact and avoiding unnecessary cross-entity coupling.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the rate limit event record.

This UUID corresponds directly to the primary key of the `todo_app_rate_limit_events` table and is used to reference or correlate this event across logs and monitoring tools.

actor_type.description:
Actor type that triggered the rate limit, such as `guestUser`, `memberUser`, or `adminUser`.

This value comes from the `actor_type` column in `todo_app_rate_limit_events` and helps distinguish whether the limit was applied to an unauthenticated guest, a signed-in member, or an administrator. It is useful for aggregating events by role and tuning different thresholds per actor category.

oneOf.description:
IP address associated with the rate limited request.

This value mirrors the `ip` column in `todo_app_rate_limit_events` and typically stores an IPv4 or IPv6 address identifying the client. It may be `null` when no IP could be reliably captured or when the limit is keyed purely by account or logical key.

Null value indicating that no IP address was stored for this event.

This occurs when the limit is not tied to a specific network address or when the IP was not available in the logging context.

ip.description:
Optional IP address to which this rate limit event applies, or null when not recorded.

When present, it enables per-IP analysis and detection of abusive clients. When null, analysis should focus on other keys such as actor identifiers or logical limit keys.

limit_key.description:
Logical key used by the rate limiting subsystem for this event.

This value mirrors the `limit_key` column in `todo_app_rate_limit_events` and can represent dimensions such as `login_identifier`, `account_id`, `ip`, or an endpoint group identifier. Operators can group events by this key to understand where throttling is concentrated.

limit_type.description:
Category of rate limit that was exceeded.

This string comes from the `limit_type` column in `todo_app_rate_limit_events` and typically includes values such as `auth_login`, `todo_write`, `admin_action`, or `global_client_limit`. It allows separate policies and monitoring per functional area of the system.

window_start.description:
Start timestamp of the rate limit window during which the threshold was exceeded.

This field is mapped from `window_start` in `todo_app_rate_limit_events`. Together with `window_end` it describes the interval for which throttling is in effect for the given key, enabling UIs to show when a client became limited.

window_end.description:
End timestamp of the rate limit window associated with this event.

This value comes from the `window_end` column in `todo_app_rate_limit_events` and indicates until when the client is expected to be throttled for the given limit key, assuming no further violations extend the window.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this rate limit event record was created.

This field corresponds to the `created_at` column in `todo_app_rate_limit_events` and represents the precise moment the system persisted the enforcement event. It is typically close to the actual request time and is used for ordering and correlating with request logs.

ITodoAppGuestUser.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a guest user identity in the todoApp service.

This DTO provides just enough information to reference or list guest users in administrative or analytical contexts without exposing full lifecycle or sensitive operational fields.

It is derived from the todo_app_guestusers Prisma model and is suitable for use inside list responses, reference properties on other DTOs, and any situation where a compact representation of a guest identity is sufficient.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the guest user.

This value is the primary key from the todo_app_guestusers table and is used to correlate any future features or logs that may reference the same conceptual guest identity.

It is generated by the system and never supplied by clients.

oneOf.description:
Display name or nickname chosen for the guest user.

This value is intended purely for human-friendly identification in logs, dashboards, or future extensions of the guest experience.

It is optional and may be null when the system has not captured any meaningful label for the guest identity.

No display name is recorded for this guest user.

Null indicates that the guest identity has no associated nickname or human-readable label.

display_name.description:
Optional display name for this guest user.

When present, it provides a human-readable nickname that can be shown in administrative tools or analytics views. When absent, the guest is typically referenced only by id or external context such as device or browser information.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this guest user record was created.

This marks the first time the system recorded this guest identity in the todo_app_guestusers table.

It can be used for ordering or for basic lifecycle analysis of guest traffic.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this guest user record was last updated.

This changes whenever mutable profile-related fields, such as display_name, are modified by the system.

It supports auditability and helps operators understand the recency of changes to the guest profile.

IPageITodoAppMemberuser.ISummary.description:
A page.

Collection of records with pagination information.

ITodoAppMemberuser.IAuthorized.description:
Authorized authentication context for a member user, returned from login, join, or refresh operations.

This DTO encapsulates the authenticated member user identity and the token information required for subsequent authenticated requests. It never exposes password or password hash fields. The id field uniquely identifies the member user account in todo_app_memberusers, while the token object contains the access (and possibly refresh) tokens and their metadata.

To minimize exposure of internal security and lifecycle state, this response includes only the essential identity attributes (id, email, optional display_name and last_login_at) and omits internal counters and audit timestamps such as failed_login_count, status, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated member user.

This corresponds to the primary key of the todo_app_memberusers record for this account and is used internally and by clients to correlate authenticated actions with a specific member user.

email.description:
Email address of the authenticated member user.

This is a safe, public identity attribute suitable for display in client applications and for use in account management flows. It must never be treated as a secret.

display_name.description:
Optional human-friendly display name for the member user.

When present, this value is taken from todo_app_memberusers.display_name and is suitable for showing in user interfaces or internal tools. When null, the UI may fall back to the email or another identifier.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the member user account.

This value is persisted in todo_app_memberusers.status and typically represents states such as active, inactive, disabled, or deleted. Business logic uses this field to decide whether the user can authenticate and operate their todo lists.

failed_login_count.description:
Number of recent consecutive failed login attempts recorded for this member account.

This field mirrors todo_app_memberusers.failed_login_count and is used primarily for monitoring and administrative debugging of authentication issues, as well as for enforcement of temporary lockouts in higher layers.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent successful login for this member user, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This field corresponds to todo_app_memberusers.last_login_at. It is null when the user has never successfully logged in and is updated whenever authentication succeeds. It is safe to expose as part of the authenticated context so that clients can show users when they last signed in.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this member user account was created, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This value comes from todo_app_memberusers.created_at and represents the initial registration time of the account.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this member user account record was last updated, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This value is taken from todo_app_memberusers.updated_at and changes whenever mutable fields such as display_name, status, or counters are modified.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp marking when this member user account was logically deleted, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This field mirrors todo_app_memberusers.deleted_at. It remains null while the account is considered active or recoverable and becomes non-null when soft deletion is applied for retention or compliance reasons.

ITodoAppMemberuser.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for querying member user accounts from the `todo_app_memberusers` table.

This DTO is used as the request body for `PATCH /todoApp/adminUser/memberUsers`, which allows administrative actors to search and browse the member user population. It encapsulates pagination controls, sorting options, and filter criteria while deliberately excluding any password or credential-related data.

Implementations should treat this object as a declarative description of the desired result set. The filters are evaluated against fields such as `email`, `status`, `created_at`, and `deleted_at` in the `todo_app_memberusers` Prisma model. When pagination and sorting properties are omitted, the backend applies sensible defaults (for example, starting from the first page with a standard page size and ordering by a commonly used timestamp).

All properties are optional so that administrators can start with a broad query and incrementally refine it by adding more filters and sort options. Validation logic must still enforce business rules such as maximum page size and valid date-time formats, returning clear errors when the request violates those constraints.

page.description:
1-based index of the result page to retrieve.

This value controls which page of results from `todo_app_memberusers` should be returned. If omitted, the backend should assume a sensible default such as `1`. Values less than `1` are considered invalid and should trigger a validation error rather than silently correcting the input.

Combined with `limit`, this property determines the offset into the full result set of matching member users.

limit.description:
Maximum number of member user records to return in a single page.

This value controls the page size for queries against `todo_app_memberusers`. The backend should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large result sets, even if the client requests a higher value. When omitted, the service applies a default page size that balances usability and performance.

Negative values are invalid and must be rejected; zero may be disallowed or treated as a special case based on business requirements but should be validated explicitly.

email.description:
Optional partial-match search criterion on the member user's email address.

This filter is applied against the `email` column of `todo_app_memberusers`, and implementations typically perform a case-insensitive `contains` or `LIKE` match. It allows administrators to locate accounts using fragments of the email, such as a domain name or a user name prefix.

When omitted, no email-based filter is applied and all matching users, regardless of email, are eligible to appear in the result set.

status.description:
Filter for member user account status.

This value is compared against the `status` column of `todo_app_memberusers`. Typical values may include states such as `active`, `inactive`, `disabled`, or `deleted`, though the exact allowed set is defined by business rules.

When provided, only accounts whose status equals the given value are included in the results. When omitted, users of all statuses are considered unless other filters constrain the set.

createdFrom.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) of the member user creation timestamp range filter.

This value is compared against the `created_at` column in `todo_app_memberusers`. Only users with `created_at` greater than or equal to this timestamp should be included in the result set.

The value must be an ISO 8601 UTC date-time string (for example, `2025-01-01T00:00:00Z`). Invalid date-time formats must be rejected with a clear validation error.

createdTo.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) of the member user creation timestamp range filter.

This value is compared against the `created_at` column in `todo_app_memberusers`. Only users with `created_at` less than or equal to this timestamp should be included in the result set.

The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or a clearly documented time zone. When used together with `createdFrom`, the backend should validate that the range is logically consistent (for example, `createdFrom` is not after `createdTo`).

deleted.description:
Flag indicating whether logically deleted accounts should be included in the result set.

This flag is evaluated against the `deleted_at` column in `todo_app_memberusers`. When `true`, users with a non-null `deleted_at` value may be included alongside active accounts. When `false` or omitted, only users whose `deleted_at` is null (that is, not logically deleted) should be returned.

This allows administrators to include soft-deleted accounts in their searches for auditing, recovery, or cleanup tasks.

orderBy.description:
Field name used to sort the member user result set.

Typical values correspond to columns in `todo_app_memberusers` such as `created_at`, `last_login_at`, or `email`. The precise list of allowed sort fields is defined by the service implementation and should be documented for API consumers.

When omitted, the backend applies a default ordering, often based on a descending `created_at` or `last_login_at` so that the most recent accounts or the most recently active users appear first.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering member user results.

Common values are `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. The exact set of supported direction keywords is defined by the service implementation and should be consistently applied across search APIs.

If this property is omitted, the backend uses its default sort direction, which is typically descending when ordering by a timestamp column so that the most recent records appear first.

ITodoAppMemberuser.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a member user account in the todoApp service.

This type is used wherever a minimal, non-sensitive view of a member user is required, such as in todo summaries, actor search results, or administrative lists. It avoids exposing any credential or security-sensitive fields while still providing enough context to identify the user in the UI.

The summary includes the account identifier and the key profile attributes that are safe to display broadly, along with status and basic activity timestamps useful for sorting and administrative inspection.

id.description:
Primary key of the member user.

This is the `id` column from the `todo_app_memberusers` table and uniquely identifies an authenticated end user who owns todos in the system.

References from other DTOs use this identifier to indicate ownership or association with a particular member account.

email.description:
Unique login identifier and contact address of the member user.

Directly corresponds to the `email` column in `todo_app_memberusers`. The value is globally unique among member accounts and is typically displayed only in contexts where the viewer is allowed to see account-level information, such as self views or administrative consoles.

It must never be treated as a secret and is not sufficient on its own for authentication flows, which always rely on credentials and tokens managed separately.

display_name.description:
Optional human-friendly display name for the member user.

This field reflects the `display_name` column from `todo_app_memberusers`. When null or blank the client may fall back to rendering the email or another derived label.

Using a dedicated display name allows users to control how their identity appears in collaborative or administrative views without changing their login identifier.

status.description:
Current account status of the member user.

Mirrors the `status` column in `todo_app_memberusers`, with typical values such as `active`, `inactive`, `disabled`, or `deleted`. Application-level rules define the exact set of allowed statuses and their meaning.

Administrative tools can use this to filter or visually distinguish accounts that are not currently allowed to sign in or that have been logically removed.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent successful login for this member user.

This value is taken from the `last_login_at` column in `todo_app_memberusers` and is null when the user has never logged in successfully.

It is useful for audit, activity dashboards, and for ordering lists of users by recency of engagement without exposing any specific session tokens or security internals.

ITodoAppMemberuser.description:
Detailed representation of a member user account stored in the todo_app_memberusers table for administrative and internal tooling views.

This DTO exposes all non-sensitive lifecycle and status fields required for operating and supervising member accounts, while strictly excluding credential material such as password_hash. It is used as the primary read model when admins inspect individual users or when other backend services need a full view of account metadata.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the member user account.

This value maps directly to todo_app_memberusers.id and is used as the primary key when referencing the user in administrative operations and internal relations.

email.description:
Unique login identifier and contact email for the member user.

This value corresponds to todo_app_memberusers.email and must be globally unique among member accounts, as it is used for authentication and for email-based communication flows.

display_name.description:
Optional human-friendly display name for the member user.

When present, this value is taken from todo_app_memberusers.display_name and is suitable for showing in user interfaces or internal tools. When null, the UI may fall back to the email or another identifier.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the member user account.

This value is persisted in todo_app_memberusers.status and typically represents states such as active, inactive, disabled, or deleted. Business logic uses this field to decide whether the user can authenticate and operate their todo lists.

failed_login_count.description:
Number of recent consecutive failed login attempts recorded for this member account.

This field mirrors todo_app_memberusers.failed_login_count and is used primarily for monitoring and administrative debugging of authentication issues, as well as for enforcement of temporary lockouts in higher layers.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent successful login for this member user, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This field corresponds to todo_app_memberusers.last_login_at. It is null when the user has never successfully logged in and is updated whenever authentication succeeds.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this member user account was created, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This value comes from todo_app_memberusers.created_at and represents the initial registration time of the account.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this member user account record was last updated, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This value is taken from todo_app_memberusers.updated_at and changes whenever mutable fields such as display_name, status, or counters are modified.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp marking when this member user account was logically deleted, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This field mirrors todo_app_memberusers.deleted_at. It remains null while the account is considered active or recoverable and becomes non-null when soft deletion is applied for retention or compliance reasons.

ITodoAppMemberuser.IUpdate.description:
Mutable subset of the member user account fields used for administrative update operations against todo_app_memberusers.

This DTO is consumed by the PUT /todoApp/adminUser/memberUsers/{memberUserId} endpoint and allows changing only those properties that are explicitly configurable through business rules, such as display information, account status, and possibly authentication-related counters. Identity, credential hash, and lifecycle timestamps are excluded from client control and remain system-managed.

email.description:
New email value for the member user account, if an admin intends to change the login identifier.

This corresponds to todo_app_memberusers.email and must remain unique among member users. Changing this email may have implications for authentication and notification flows and therefore should be used carefully by administrative tools.

display_name.description:
Updated human-friendly display name for the member user.

When provided, this value will be written to todo_app_memberusers.display_name. Supplying null clears the display name so that UIs may fall back to email or another identifier.

status.description:
Updated lifecycle status of the member user account.

This value maps to todo_app_memberusers.status and is used by business logic to enable or restrict access. Typical changes include activating, deactivating, or disabling an account according to operational and compliance rules.

failed_login_count.description:
Administrative override of the failed login counter for this member account.

When set, this value updates todo_app_memberusers.failed_login_count and can be used, for example, to reset the counter after resolving authentication issues or to enforce a specific lockout-related value.
